title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第二十: 王珪 戴冑 岑文本 杜正倫
title.en: Volume 70 Biographies 20: Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, Cen Wenben, Du Zhenglun
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第二十: 王珪 戴冑 岑文本 杜正倫 Volume 70 Biographies 20: Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, Cen Wenben, Du Zhenglun

sentences.zh: 王珪 戴胄 兄子至德

translations.literal: Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, nephew Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, and Zhide, nephew of the latter.

sentences.zh: 岑文本 兄子長倩 倩子羲 格輔元附

translations.literal: Cen Wenben, nephew Changqian, Changqian's son Xi, with Ge Fuyuan appended.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben; his nephew Changqian; Changqian's son Xi; with Ge Fuyuan appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 杜正倫

translations.literal: Du Zhenglun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun.

sentences.zh: 王珪，字叔玠，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, courtesy name Shujie, was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, whose courtesy name was Shujie, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 在魏為烏丸氏，曾祖神念，自魏奔梁，復姓王氏。

translations.literal: In Wei [the family] was of the Wuhuan clan; his great-grandfather Shennian fled from Wei to Liang and restored the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei they had been of the Wuhuan clan; his great-grandfather Shennian fled from Wei to Liang and took back the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 祖僧辯，梁太尉、尚書令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengbian was Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbian had served Liang as Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父顗，北齊樂陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Administrator of Leling in Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been Administrator of Leling under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 珪幼孤，性雅澹，少嗜欲，志量沉深，能安於貧賤，體道履正，交不苟合。

translations.literal: Gui was orphaned in childhood; his nature was refined and calm, with few desires; his will was profound and deep; he could rest content in poverty and low station, embodying the Way and walking in rectitude, and did not make acquaintances carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Gui lost his parents young. Refined and self-contained, he cared little for worldly pleasures; his resolve ran deep, and he could live at ease in poverty. He held to the Way in conduct and would not strike up friendships lightly.

sentences.zh: 季叔頗，當時通儒，有人倫之鑑，嘗謂所親曰：「門戶所寄，唯在此兒耳。」

translations.literal: His uncle Bo, a leading scholar of the time with a discerning eye for human worth, once said to those close to him: "The hopes of our house rest on this boy alone.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Bo, a leading scholar of the day with a keen eye for character, once told those close to him, "Our family's hopes rest on this boy alone.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era he served as Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang reign he was appointed Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及頗坐漢王諒反事被誅，珪當從坐，遂亡命於南山，積十餘歲。

translations.literal: When Bo was executed for involvement in Prince Liang of Han's rebellion, Gui was liable to share the punishment and therefore fled into hiding on Mount Nan, where he remained more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was put to death for his part in Prince Liang of Han's rebellion, Gui faced punishment as an associate and fled into hiding on Mount Nan, where he stayed for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，丞相府司錄李綱薦珪貞諒有器識，引為世子府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the Pass, Li Gang, Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, recommended Gui as upright, trustworthy, and possessed of talent and insight, and he was appointed Adviser in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu entered the Pass, Li Gang, registrar of the chancellor's office, praised Gui's integrity and ability and had him made adviser in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 及東宮建，除太子中舍人；

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was set up, he was made attendant to the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 尋轉中允，甚為太子所禮。

translations.literal: soon afterward he was transferred to Junior Mentor and was greatly honored by the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: and soon after was promoted to junior mentor, winning great favor from the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 後以連其陰謀事，流於巂州。

translations.literal: Later, because of his connection with the heir apparent's conspiracy, he was banished to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, implicated in the heir apparent's conspiracy, he was exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 建成誅後，太宗素知其才，召拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After Jian Cheng was executed, Taizong had long known his talent and summoned him, appointing him Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian Cheng's execution, Taizong, who had long known his worth, summoned him and made him remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，太宗嘗謂侍臣曰：「正主御邪臣，不能致理；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Taizong once said to his attending ministers: "An upright ruler governing wicked ministers cannot bring order;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Taizong once told his ministers, "An upright ruler with wicked ministers cannot bring good government;

sentences.zh: 正臣事邪主，亦不能致理，唯君臣相遇，有同魚水，則海內可安也。

translations.literal: upright ministers serving a wicked ruler also cannot bring order; only when ruler and minister meet like fish and water can the realm within the seas be secure.
translations.idiomatic: nor can upright ministers serving a wicked ruler; only when ruler and minister meet like fish and water can the realm be at peace.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖，田舍翁耳。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han was but a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han had been nothing but a farmer.

sentences.zh: 提三尺劍定天下，既而規模弘遠，慶流子孫者，此蓋任得賢臣所致也。

translations.literal: He took up a three-foot sword and settled the realm; thereafter his grand design was far-reaching and his blessings flowed to his descendants — this was surely because he employed worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he took up a sword and conquered the realm, and afterward his vision proved vast and his blessings reached his descendants — all because he put worthy ministers in office.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不明，幸諸公數相匡救，冀憑嘉謀，致天下於太平耳。」

translations.literal: Although I am not enlightened, I am fortunate that you gentlemen repeatedly correct and rescue me; I hope by your excellent counsel to bring the realm to peace.
translations.idiomatic: I may not be enlightened, but you gentlemen have often set me right; I hope through your good counsel to bring the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 珪對曰：「臣聞木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Gui replied: "Your subject has heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight, and a ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied, "I have heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight, and a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 故古者聖主，必有諍臣七人，言而不用，則相繼以死。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity sage rulers always had seven remonstrating ministers; if their words were not heeded, they died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, sage rulers kept seven remonstrating ministers; if their counsel went unheeded, they died one after another.

sentences.zh: 陛下開聖慮，納芻蕘，臣處不諱之朝，實願罄其狂瞽。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has opened your sage understanding and accepted humble counsel; your subject stands in a court where nothing is taboo and truly wishes to exhaust his reckless blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has opened your mind to humble counsel; I serve in a court where nothing is taboo, and I wish to offer all the folly I can muster.

sentences.zh: 太宗稱善，敕自今後中書門下及三品以上入閣，必遣諫官隨之。

translations.literal: Taizong praised this and ordered that from then on, whenever ministers of the third rank and above of the Secretariat and Chancellery entered the inner court, remonstrating officials must accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and ordered that whenever Secretariat and Chancellery officials of the third rank and above entered the inner court, remonstrating officials must accompany them.

sentences.zh: 珪每推誠納忠，多所獻替，太宗顧待益厚，賜爵永寧縣男，遷黃門侍郎，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Gui always offered sincerity and loyal counsel, making many proposals for improvement and rejection; Taizong's regard for him grew ever deeper; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning County and promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, while also serving as Junior Mentor on the Right to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui spoke with candor and loyalty, offering many suggestions for improvement; Taizong favored him ever more, enfeoffed him as baron of Yongning County, promoted him to vice director of the palace secretariat, and made him junior mentor on the right to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，代高士廉為侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year he replaced Gao Shilian as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he replaced Gao Shilian as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗閒居，與珪宴語，時有美人侍側，本廬江王瑗之姬，瑗敗籍沒入宮，太宗指示之曰：「廬江不道，賊殺其夫而納其室。

translations.literal: Taizong was once at leisure, dining and conversing with Gui; a beautiful woman waited at his side — originally a concubine of Prince Yuan of Lujiang; when Yuan was defeated she was registered and taken into the palace. Taizong pointed to her and said: "Lujiang was without the Way; like a bandit he killed her husband and took her into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at leisure, Taizong was dining and talking with Gui when a beautiful woman stood beside him — formerly a concubine of Prince Yuan of Lujiang. After Yuan's defeat she had been seized for the palace. Taizong pointed to her and said, "Lujiang was lawless: like a bandit he killed her husband and took her for himself.

sentences.zh: 暴虐之甚，何有不亡者乎！」

translations.literal: His cruelty and violence were so extreme — how could he not perish!
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty was so extreme — how could he not fall!

sentences.zh: 珪避席曰：「陛下以廬江取此婦人為是耶，為非耶？」

translations.literal: Gui left his seat and said: "Does Your Majesty regard Lujiang's taking of this woman as right, or as wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose from his seat and said, "Does Your Majesty think Lujiang was right to take this woman, or wrong?"

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「殺人而取其妻，卿乃問朕是非，何也？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "He killed a man and took his wife — yet you ask me whether it was right or wrong. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "He killed a man and took his wife — and you ask me whether that was right or wrong? Why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞於管子曰：『齊桓公之郭，問其父老曰：『郭何故亡？』

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject has heard in Guanzi that when Duke Huan of Qi reached Guo, he asked the elders: 'Why did Guo perish?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have read in Guanzi that when Duke Huan of Qi reached Guo, he asked the elders, 'Why did Guo perish?

sentences.zh: 父老曰：『以其善善而惡惡也。』

translations.literal: The elders said: 'Because he was good to the good and hostile to the wicked.'
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'Because he was good to the good and hostile to the wicked.'

sentences.zh: 桓公曰：『若子之言，乃賢君也，何至於亡？』

translations.literal: Duke Huan said: 'By your words, he was a worthy ruler — how could he have perished?'
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'By your account he was a worthy ruler — how could he have perished?'

sentences.zh: 父老曰：『不然，郭君善善而不能用，惡惡而不能去，所以亡也。』

translations.literal: The elders said: 'Not so. The lord of Guo was good to the good but could not employ them, and hostile to the wicked but could not remove them — that is why he perished.'
translations.idiomatic: They said, 'Not so. The lord of Guo favored the good but could not employ them, hated the wicked but could not remove them — that is why he perished.'

sentences.zh: 今此婦人尚在左右，竊以聖心為是之，陛下若以為非，此謂知惡而不去也。」

translations.literal: This woman is still at Your Majesty's side; I venture to think the sage heart approves of her. If Your Majesty regards it as wrong, this is knowing what is wicked yet not removing it.'
translations.idiomatic: This woman is still at Your Majesty's side; I fear Your Majesty approves of her. If Your Majesty thinks it wrong yet keeps her, that is knowing evil and not removing it.'

sentences.zh: 太宗雖不出此美人，而甚重其言。

translations.literal: Although Taizong did not dismiss this beautiful woman, he greatly valued Gui's words.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong did not dismiss the woman, but he valued Gui's words highly.

sentences.zh: 時太常少卿祖孝孫以教宮人聲樂不稱旨，為太宗所讓。

translations.literal: At that time Zu Xiaosun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was reproached by Taizong because the palace women's music instruction did not please him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zu Xiaosun, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was rebuked by Taizong because the palace women's musical training did not satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 珪及溫彥博諫曰：「孝孫妙解音律，非不用心，但恐陛下顧問不得其人，以惑陛下視聽。

translations.literal: Gui and Wen Yanbo remonstrated: "Xiaosun has a subtle mastery of pitch and mode; it is not that he is inattentive — but I fear Your Majesty's advisers are not the right men and are misleading Your Majesty's sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Wen Yanbo remonstrated, "Xiaosun understands music profoundly; he is not negligent in his duties — but I fear Your Majesty is being misled by the wrong advisers.

sentences.zh: 且孝孫雅士，陛下忽為教女樂而怪之，臣恐天下怪愕。」

translations.literal: Moreover Xiaosun is a refined gentleman; Your Majesty suddenly blames him for teaching women's music — your subjects fear the realm will be astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xiaosun is a refined gentleman; if Your Majesty blames him for teaching women's music, I fear the realm will be astonished.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒曰：「卿皆我之腹心，當進忠獻直，何乃附下罔上，反為孝孫言也！」

translations.literal: Taizong angrily said: "You are all my inner confidants and ought to advance loyalty and offer straight counsel — why do you side with inferiors to deceive your superiors and speak instead for Xiaosun!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said angrily, "You are all my closest advisers and ought to speak loyal, straight truth — why do you side with inferiors against your lord and speak up for Xiaosun?"

sentences.zh: 彥博拜謝，珪獨不拜。

translations.literal: Yanbo bowed in apology; Gui alone did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo bowed in apology; Gui alone did not.

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣本事前宮，罪已當死。

translations.literal: He said: "Your subject formerly served the former palace; my crime already deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I once served the former heir apparent; my crime already deserved death.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜恕性命，不以不肖，置之樞近，責以忠直。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pitied and spared my life, and despite my unworthiness placed me near the pivot of power, charging me with loyalty and straight dealing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spared my life and, despite my unworthiness, placed me near the center of power, charging me with loyalty and candor.

sentences.zh: 今臣所言，豈是為私？

translations.literal: What your subject says now — is it for private ends?
translations.idiomatic: What I say now — is it for private ends?

sentences.zh: 不意陛下忽以疑事誚臣，是陛下負臣，臣不負陛下。」

translations.literal: I did not expect Your Majesty suddenly to reproach your subject on a doubtful matter — it is Your Majesty who has failed your subject; your subject has not failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect Your Majesty suddenly to reproach me on suspicion — it is Your Majesty who has failed me, not I who have failed Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝默然而罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝謂房玄齡曰：「自古帝王，能納諫者固難矣。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor said to Fang Xuanling: "Since antiquity it has indeed been difficult for emperors to accept remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to Fang Xuanling, "Since antiquity it has been hard for rulers to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 昔周武王尚不用伯夷、叔齊，宣王賢主，杜伯猶以無罪見殺，吾夙夜庶幾前聖，恨不能仰及古人。

translations.literal: In former times even King Wu of Zhou did not employ Boyi and Shuqi; King Xuan was a worthy ruler, yet Duke Du was still killed though guiltless. I day and night hope to approach the former sages, yet regret that I cannot look up to the men of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Even King Wu of Zhou did not employ Boyi and Shuqi; King Xuan was a worthy ruler, yet Duke Du was killed though innocent. I strive day and night to emulate the sages of old, yet regret that I cannot measure up to them.

sentences.zh: 昨責彥博、王珪，朕甚悔之。

translations.literal: Yesterday, in reproaching Yanbo and Wang Gui, I deeply regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, in rebuking Yanbo and Wang Gui, I was deeply in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 公等勿以此而不進直言也。」

translations.literal: Do not on this account fail to advance straight words."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let this keep you from speaking straight truth."

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡、李靖、溫彥博、戴胄、魏徵與珪同知國政。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling, Li Jing, Wen Yanbo, Dai Zhou, Wei Zheng, and Gui jointly directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Xuanling, Li Jing, Wen Yanbo, Dai Zhou, Wei Zheng, and Gui shared direction of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 後嘗侍宴，太宗謂珪曰：「卿識鑑清通，尤善談論，自房玄齡等，咸宜品藻，又可自量，孰與諸子賢？」

translations.literal: Later, when attending a banquet, Taizong said to Gui: "Your discernment is clear and penetrating, and you are especially skilled in discussion. Starting with Fang Xuanling and the rest, you ought all to be appraised; you may also measure yourself — who among these men is the worthiest?
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a banquet, Taizong said to Gui, "Your judgment is keen and you are especially skilled in debate. Appraise Fang Xuanling and the others — and yourself as well: who among them is the worthiest?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「孜孜奉國，知無不為，臣不如玄齡；

translations.literal: He replied: "In diligent service to the state, knowing nothing he would not do — your subject is not the equal of Xuanling;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In tireless service to the state, leaving nothing undone — I am not the equal of Xuanling;

sentences.zh: 才兼文武，出將入相，臣不如李靖；

translations.literal: in talent combining civil and military, going forth as general and entering as minister — your subject is not the equal of Li Jing;
translations.idiomatic: in talent combining civil and military, going forth as general and entering as minister — I am not the equal of Li Jing;

sentences.zh: 敷奏詳明，出納惟允，臣不如溫彥博；

translations.literal: in presenting memorials with detail and clarity, in intake and output always fitting — your subject is not the equal of Wen Yanbo;
translations.idiomatic: in presenting memorials with clarity and precision, in intake and output always fitting — I am not the equal of Wen Yanbo;

sentences.zh: 處繁理劇，眾務必舉，臣不如戴胄；

translations.literal: in handling complexity and managing urgency, in all affairs certain to accomplish them — your subject is not the equal of Dai Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: in handling complexity and urgency, accomplishing every task — I am not the equal of Dai Zhou;

sentences.zh: 以諫諍為心，恥君不及於堯、舜，臣不如魏徵。

translations.literal: in taking remonstrance as his heart, ashamed that his lord falls short of Yao and Shun — your subject is not the equal of Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: in taking remonstrance to heart, ashamed when his lord falls short of Yao and Shun — I am not the equal of Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 至如激濁揚清，嫉惡好善，臣於數子，亦有一日之長。」

translations.literal: As for stirring the muddy and lifting the clear, hating evil and loving good — your subject among these several men also has his day of superiority.
translations.idiomatic: As for stirring the muddy and lifting the clear, hating evil and loving good — among these men I too have my day of superiority.

sentences.zh: 太宗深然其言，群公亦各以為盡己所懷，謂之確論。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply approved his words; the assembled lords each felt he had fully expressed what was in their hearts and called it a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong strongly approved; the assembled ministers each felt he had spoken their own minds, and called it a sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 七年，坐漏洩禁中語，左遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for leaking forbidden words from within the palace, he was demoted to Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for leaking forbidden palace talk, he was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled and made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與諸儒正定《五禮》，書成，賜帛三百段，封一子為縣男。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with various Confucian scholars he fixed the 《Five Rites》; when the book was completed he was granted three hundred bolts of silk and one son was enfeoffed as Baron of a county.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, working with Confucian scholars, he helped fix the 《Five Rites》; when the work was done he received three hundred bolts of silk and one son was enfeoffed as baron of a county.

sentences.zh: 是歲，兼魏王師。

translations.literal: That year he also served as tutor to the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year he also became tutor to the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 既而上問黃門侍郎韋挺曰：「王珪為魏王泰師，與其相見，若為禮節？」

translations.literal: Thereafter the Emperor questioned Vice Director Wei Ting of the Palace Secretariat: "Wang Gui is tutor to the Prince of Wei Tai — when he meets him, what should the ritual observance be?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked Vice Director Wei Ting of the palace secretariat, "Wang Gui is tutor to Prince Tai of Wei — what ritual should govern their meetings?

sentences.zh: 挺對曰：「見師之禮，拜答如禮。」

translations.literal: Ting replied: "The ritual for meeting one's teacher — bowing and responding according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "The ritual for meeting one's teacher: bowing and responding as ritual requires."

sentences.zh: 王問珪以忠孝，珪答曰：「陛下，王之君也，事君思盡忠；

translations.literal: The Prince questioned Gui on loyalty and filial piety; Gui answered: "Your Majesty is the Prince's lord — in serving his lord he should think of exhausting loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Gui about loyalty and filial piety; Gui answered, "Your Majesty is the prince's sovereign — in serving his sovereign he should think only of loyalty;

sentences.zh: 陛下，王之父也，事父思盡孝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the Prince's father — in serving his father he should think of exhausting filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the prince's father — in serving his father he should think only of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 忠孝之道，可以立身，可以成名，當年可以享天祐，余芳可以垂後葉。」

translations.literal: The way of loyalty and filial piety can establish the person, can make a name, in one's own years can enjoy Heaven's blessing, and its lingering fragrance can extend to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The way of loyalty and filial piety can establish a man and win him a name; in his own lifetime he may enjoy Heaven's blessing, and its fragrance may reach later generations.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「忠孝之道，已聞教矣，願聞所習。」

translations.literal: The Prince said: "On the way of loyalty and filial piety I have already received instruction; I wish to hear what one should practice."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I have been taught the way of loyalty and filial piety; I wish to hear what I should practice."

sentences.zh: 珪答曰：「漢東平王蒼云：『為善最樂。』」

translations.literal: Gui answered: "The Eastern Prince of Ping of Han, Liu Cang, said: 'Doing good is the greatest joy.'
translations.idiomatic: Gui answered, "Liu Cang, Eastern Prince of Ping of Han, said, 'Doing good is the greatest joy.'

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「古來帝子，生於宮闥，及其成人，無不驕逸，是以傾覆相踵，少能自濟。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to his attending ministers: "Since antiquity imperial sons, born within the palace gates, when they reach adulthood are without exception arrogant and dissolute; hence ruin has followed ruin in succession, and few have been able to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Since antiquity imperial sons, born within the palace, have almost all grown up arrogant and dissolute; ruin has followed ruin, and few have saved themselves.

sentences.zh: 我今嚴教子弟，欲令皆得安全。

translations.literal: I now strictly instruct my sons and younger brothers, wishing to make them all secure.
translations.idiomatic: I now instruct my sons and younger brothers strictly, hoping to keep them all safe.

sentences.zh: 王珪我久驅使，是所諳悉，以其意存忠孝，選為子師。

translations.literal: Wang Gui I have long employed and am well acquainted with; because his mind holds loyalty and filial piety, I have chosen him as the Prince's tutor.
translations.idiomatic: I have long employed Wang Gui and know him well; because his heart holds loyalty and filial piety, I have chosen him as the prince's tutor.

sentences.zh: 爾宜語泰：『汝之待珪，如事我也，可以無過。』」

translations.literal: You ought to tell Tai: 'In how you treat Gui, treat him as you would treat me — then you may be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: You should tell Tai, 'Treat Gui as you would treat me, and you will not go wrong.

sentences.zh: 泰每為之先拜，珪亦以師道自居，物議善之。

translations.literal: Tai each time bowed to him first; Gui also took the teacher's way as his station — public opinion approved."
translations.idiomatic: Tai always bowed to him first; Gui likewise held to the teacher's role — and public opinion approved."

sentences.zh: 時珪子敬直尚南平公主。

translations.literal: At that time Gui's son Jingzhi was married to the Princess of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gui's son Jingzhi was married to the Princess of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 禮有婦見舅姑之儀，自近代公主出降，此禮皆廢。

translations.literal: Ritual provides the ceremony of a wife meeting her husband's parents; since recent times, when princesses marry down, this ritual has all been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual prescribes a ceremony in which a wife meets her husband's parents; since recent times, when princesses married commoners, this ceremony had been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「今主上欽明，動循法制。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Now the sovereign is reverent and enlightened, and in every action follows law and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Our sovereign is reverent and enlightened and follows law in every action.

sentences.zh: 吾受公主謁見，豈為身榮，所以成國家之美耳。」

translations.literal: That I receive the princess's visit — is it for my personal glory? It is to complete the state's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: That I receive the princess's visit is not for my personal glory but to complete the state's dignity.

sentences.zh: 遂與其妻就席而坐，令公主親執笄行盥饋之道，禮成而退。

translations.literal: He and his wife thereupon took their seats; he had the princess personally hold the hairpin and perform the washing and feeding rites; when the ritual was complete she withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife took their seats and had the princess personally perform the hairpin, washing, and feeding rites; when the ceremony was done she withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是後公主下降有舅姑者，皆備婦禮，自珪始也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when princesses married down to households with parents-in-law, they all observed the wife's rites — beginning with Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when princesses married into families with parents-in-law, they all observed the wife's rites — beginning with Gui.

sentences.zh: 珪少時貧寒，人或遺之，初不辭謝；

translations.literal: When Gui was young he was poor and cold; when people gave him gifts he at first never declined or thanked them;
translations.idiomatic: When young, Gui was poor; when people gave him gifts he never declined or thanked them;

sentences.zh: 及貴，皆厚報之，雖其人已亡，必賑贍其妻子。

translations.literal: when he became eminent he repaid them all generously; even if the giver had died, he was certain to relieve and support his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: when he rose high he repaid them all generously; even if the giver had died, he supported his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 事寡嫂盡禮，撫孤侄恩義極隆，宗姻困匱者，亦多所周恤。

translations.literal: He served his widowed sister-in-law with full ritual; in nurturing his orphaned nephews his kindness and righteousness were utmost; among clan and affinal kin in hardship and want, he also gave much relief.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his widowed sister-in-law with full ritual propriety, showed utmost kindness to his orphaned nephews, and gave generously to needy kin.

sentences.zh: 珪通貴漸久，而不營私廟，四時蒸嘗，猶祭於寢。

translations.literal: Gui had been eminent for a long time yet did not build a private ancestral temple; for the seasonal offerings he still sacrificed in his bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: Though long eminent, Gui had not built a private ancestral temple and still offered seasonal sacrifices in his bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 坐為法司所劾，太宗優容，弗之譴也，因為立廟，以愧其心。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the law office; Taizong treated him with forbearance and did not reproach him, but had a temple built for him to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The law office impeached him; Taizong was lenient and did not reproach him, but had a temple built for him to stir his conscience.

sentences.zh: 珪既儉不中禮，時論以是少之。

translations.literal: Gui was frugal to the point of not conforming to ritual, and contemporary opinion on this account thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's frugality fell short of ritual propriety, and opinion held this against him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遇疾，敕公主就第省視，又遣民部尚書唐儉增損藥膳。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he fell ill; an edict ordered the princess to visit his residence to inquire after him, and Minister of Population Tang Jian was also sent to adjust his medicines and food.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he fell ill; the emperor ordered the princess to visit his home and sent Minister of Population Tang Jian to adjust his medicines and diet.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太宗素服舉哀於別次，悼惜久之。

translations.literal: Taizong in plain robes performed mourning in a separate chamber and grieved for him a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned in plain robes in a side chamber and grieved for him at length.

sentences.zh: 詔魏王泰率百官親往臨哭，贈吏部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Prince of Wei Tai to lead the hundred officials in person to attend the mourning wail; he was posthumously appointed Minister of the Civil Office and given the posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince Tai of Wei to lead the officials in person to mourn; Gui was posthumously made minister of the civil office with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子崇基，襲爵，官至主爵郎中。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chongji inherited the enfeoffment and rose to Master of Enfeoffments in the Bureau of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chongji inherited the title and rose to master of enfeoffments in the bureau of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 少子敬直，以尚主拜附馬都尉，坐與太子承乾交結，徙於嶺外。

translations.literal: His younger son Jingzhi, through marriage to a princess, was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry; for association with the Heir Apparent Chenggan he was banished beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Jingzhi, through marriage to a princess, became commandant of escort cavalry; for associating with the heir apparent Chenggan he was exiled beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 崇基孫旭，開元初，為左司郎中，兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Chongji's grandson Xu, at the beginning of Kaiyuan, served as Master of the Left Department and concurrently as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji's grandson Xu, at the beginning of Kaiyuan, was master of the left department and concurrently attending censor.

sentences.zh: 時光祿少卿盧崇道犯罪配流嶺南，逃歸匿於東都，為讎家所發。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Chongdao, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, was convicted and banished to Lingnan; he fled back and hid in the Eastern Capital, and was exposed by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Chongdao, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, had been convicted and banished to Lingnan; he fled back and hid in the Eastern Capital, where an enemy family exposed him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令旭究其獄，旭欲擅其威權，因捕系崇道親黨數十人，皆極其楚毒，然後結成其罪，崇道及其三子並坐死，親友皆決杖流貶。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Xu to investigate the case; Xu wished to monopolize authority and power, and therefore arrested and imprisoned several tens of Chongdao's kin and associates, all subjected to extreme torture, and only then framed their guilt; Chongdao and his three sons were all sentenced to death, and kin and friends were all beaten with the rod and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ordered Xu to investigate; Xu sought to monopolize power, arrested dozens of Chongdao's kin and associates, tortured them severely, and only then framed their guilt. Chongdao and his three sons were all put to death; kin and friends were beaten and banished.

sentences.zh: 時得罪多是知名之士，四海冤之。

translations.literal: At that time those convicted were mostly men of renown, and the realm within the four seas considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those convicted were well-known men, and the realm considered it a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 旭又與御史大夫李傑不協，遞相糾訐，傑竟坐左遷衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xu also was at odds with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie; they repeatedly impeached each other, and Jie in the end was demoted to Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu also clashed with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie; they impeached each other in turn, and Jie was eventually demoted to prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 旭既得志，擅行威福，由是朝廷畏而鄙之。

translations.literal: Once Xu had gotten his wish, he arbitrarily wielded authority and bestowed favors; hence the court both feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu had his way, he abused his power at will, and the court came to both fear and despise him.

sentences.zh: 俄以贓罪黜為龍川尉，憤恚而死，甚為時之所快。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed for bribery and demoted to Commandant of Longchuan; he died of rage and resentment, which greatly pleased people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was stripped of office for corruption and demoted to commandant of Longchuan. He died consumed by fury, to the great satisfaction of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicature.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1, he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Judicature.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書長孫無忌嘗被召，不解佩刀入東上閣。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Personnel Zhangsun Wuji was once summoned; without removing the sword he wore, he entered the Eastern Upper Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Personnel Zhangsun Wuji was summoned on one occasion, he entered the Eastern Upper Pavilion without first removing his sword.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射封德彝議以監門校尉不覺，罪當死；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi proposed that the gate-monitor commandant, for failing to notice, should be guilty of a crime warranting death;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi argued that the gate-monitor commandant who had failed to notice ought to be sentenced to death;

sentences.zh: 無忌誤帶入，罰銅二十斤。

translations.literal: Wuji, who had carried it in by mistake, should pay a fine of twenty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji, who had brought the sword in by mistake, should pay a fine of twenty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this proposal.

sentences.zh: 胄駁曰：「校尉不覺與無忌帶入，同為誤耳。

translations.literal: Zhou rebutted, saying: "The commandant's failure to notice and Wuji's carrying it in are both mistakes alike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou objected: "The commandant's failure to notice and Wuji's bringing the sword in are equally errors.

sentences.zh: 臣子之於尊極，不得稱誤，准律云：『供御湯藥、飲食、舟船，誤不知者，皆死。』

translations.literal: Regarding subjects toward the supreme ruler, one may not call it a mistake. According to the law it says: 'For supplying the imperial bath medicine, food and drink, or boats and ships--if through mistake one does not know, all are death.
translations.idiomatic: Before the sovereign, a subject cannot plead mere error. The code states: "Anyone who through inadvertence supplies improper imperial medicines, food, drink, or vessels--all such cases carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下若錄其功，非憲司所決；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty records his merit, it is not for the judicial offices to decide;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty chooses to credit his service, that lies outside the courts' authority;

sentences.zh: 若當據法，罰銅未為得衷。」

translations.literal: If one must apply the law, a fine of copper is not getting the mean right."
translations.idiomatic: but if the law must be applied as written, a copper fine does not strike the proper balance.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「法者，非朕一人之法，乃天下之法也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "Law is not the law of me alone--it is the law of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "The law is not mine alone--it is the law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 何得以無忌國之親戚，便欲阿之？」

translations.literal: How can it be that because Wuji is a kinsman of the state, you immediately wish to favor him?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you seek to shield Wuji merely because he is the emperor's kinsman?

sentences.zh: 更令定議。

translations.literal: He ordered them to reconsider and settle the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to reconsider and reach a final decision.

sentences.zh: 德彝執議如初，太宗將從其議，胄又曰：「校尉緣無忌以致罪，於法當輕。

translations.literal: Deyi held to his original view; Taizong was about to follow his proposal when Zhou again said: "The commandant incurred guilt because of Wuji--under the law the sentence should be lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi held firm to his original position, and Taizong was on the point of accepting it when Zhou spoke again: "The commandant was punished only because of Wuji; under the law his sentence should be lighter.

sentences.zh: 若論其誤，則為情一也，而生死頓殊，敢以固請。」

translations.literal: If one discusses their mistake, the circumstances are the same, yet life and death are suddenly different--I venture to press my request firmly."
translations.idiomatic: If both acts were errors, the circumstances are the same, yet one man lives and another dies. I earnestly beg you to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，竟免校尉之死。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and in the end exempted the commandant from death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and in the end spared the commandant's life.

sentences.zh: 於時朝廷盛開選舉，或有詐偽資廕者，帝令其自首，不首者罪至於死。

translations.literal: At that time the court widely opened selection and appointment; some there were who fraudulently claimed yin privileges. The Emperor ordered them to confess voluntarily--those who did not confess would be guilty of a crime punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then holding large-scale examinations and appointments, and some candidates had falsified hereditary privilege claims. The emperor decreed that they confess; anyone who did not would face the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 俄有詐偽者事洩，胄據法斷流以奏之。

translations.literal: Soon a fraudster's matter was exposed; Zhou applied the law and sentenced exile, then submitted the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon one such fraud came to light. Zhou applied the statute, sentenced the man to exile, and submitted the case.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕下敕不首者死，今斷從流，是示天下以不信。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I issued an edict that those who did not confess would die; now you sentence him to exile--is this not showing all under Heaven that I am not to be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I decreed death for anyone who failed to confess, yet you sentence this man to exile. Will this not tell the empire that my word cannot be trusted?

sentences.zh: 卿欲賣獄乎？」

translations.literal: Do you wish to sell judgments?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you trying to sell justice?

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「陛下當即殺之，非臣所及。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "Your Majesty should execute him immediately--that is beyond my authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou replied, "Your Majesty could execute him at once--that lies beyond my authority.

sentences.zh: 既付所司，臣不敢虧法。」

translations.literal: Since he has been entrusted to the relevant office, I dare not violate the law."
translations.idiomatic: But once the case was entrusted to my office, I could not bend the law.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿自守法，而令我失信邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You keep the law yourself, but make me lose trust, do you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You uphold the law, but would you have me break my word?"

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「法者，國家所以布大信於天下；

translations.literal: Zhou said: "Law is what the state uses to spread great trust throughout all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "The law is how the state establishes its greatest credibility with the empire;

sentences.zh: 言者，當時喜怒之所發耳。

translations.literal: words are merely what momentary joy or anger sends forth.
translations.idiomatic: words are spoken in the heat of a moment's anger.

sentences.zh: 陛下發一朝之忿而許殺之，既知不可而置之於法，此乃忍小忿而存大信也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, moved by a morning's wrath, promised to execute him; now knowing it cannot be done yet placing him under law--this is restraining small anger and preserving great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in a burst of anger, vowed to kill him; now that you know the law forbids it, you defer to the statute. That is to swallow a moment's wrath and preserve the empire's trust.

sentences.zh: 若順忿違信，臣竊為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: If you follow anger and violate trust, I privately regret this for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: If you indulged your anger and forfeited that trust, I would deeply regret it for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「法有所失，公能正之，朕何憂也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When the law errs, you can correct it--what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the law goes astray, you set it right. What have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 胄前後犯顏執法多此類。

translations.literal: Before and after, Zhou's facing the throne to uphold law was many times of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again Zhou defied the throne to uphold the law in just this fashion.

sentences.zh: 所論刑獄，皆事無冤濫，隨方指擿，言如泉湧。

translations.literal: In the criminal cases he discussed, none involved wrongful or excessive punishment; pointing out faults as each case required, his words flowed like a spring.
translations.idiomatic: The cases he reviewed were free of wrongful conviction or excessive punishment; he identified every flaw as the facts required, and his arguments poured forth like a spring.

sentences.zh: 其年，轉尚書右丞，尋遷左丞。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; soon after he was promoted to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became right assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon after was promoted to left assistant director.

sentences.zh: 先是，每歲水旱，皆以正倉出給，無倉之處，就食他州，百姓多致飢乏。

translations.literal: Before this, in every year's flood or drought, grain was issued from the principal granaries; where there were no granaries, people went to other provinces for food, and the common people often fell into hunger and deprivation.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in years of flood or drought the government issued grain from state granaries; where no granary existed, people had to seek food in other provinces, and many commoners were left hungry and destitute.

sentences.zh: 二年，胄上言：「水旱凶災，前聖之所不免。

translations.literal: In the second year Zhou submitted a memorial saying: "Floods, droughts, and disastrous calamities are what former sages could not avoid.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhou memorialized the throne: "Floods, drought, and famine are calamities even the sage kings could not always prevent.

sentences.zh: 國無九年儲蓄，禮經之所明誡。

translations.literal: That a state lacks nine years' stores is what the Classics of Rites clearly admonishes against.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites clearly warn that a state should not go without nine years' reserves.

sentences.zh: 今喪亂已後，戶口凋殘，每歲納租，未實倉稟。

translations.literal: Now after the turmoil of war and disorder, registered households are depleted and damaged; each year's tax grain is paid in but does not truly fill the granary stores.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars, the population has been decimated; the grain collected as tax each year scarcely fills the granaries.

sentences.zh: 隨即出給，才供當年，若有凶災，將何賑恤？

translations.literal: It is immediately issued out, barely supplying the current year--if there is a disastrous calamity, with what will one grant relief?
translations.idiomatic: It is disbursed at once and barely covers the year's needs. When disaster strikes, what will remain for relief?

sentences.zh: 故隋開皇立制，天下之人，節級輸粟，名為社倉，終文皇代，得無饑饉。

translations.literal: Therefore Sui in Kaihuang established a system: people throughout the realm paid grain by graduated levels, called "communal granaries"--through the end of Emperor Wen's reign there were no famines.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era the Sui established a system whereby people throughout the realm paid grain in graded amounts into communal granaries; throughout Emperor Wen's reign the land knew no famine.

sentences.zh: 及大業中年，國用不足，並取社倉之物以充官費，故至末途，無以支給。

translations.literal: By the middle of the Daye reign, state expenses were insufficient; they all took the communal granaries' goods to meet official costs, so that by the final stretch there was nothing with which to supply relief.
translations.idiomatic: By the middle of the Daye reign, however, the treasury ran short and the communal stores were raided to meet official expenses, until in the dynasty's final years there was nothing left to disburse.

sentences.zh: 自王公已下，爰及眾庶，計所墾田稼穡頃畝，每至秋熟，准其苗以理勸課，盡令出粟。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes down to the common multitude, calculating the qing and mu of land they had opened for farming, each time autumn ripened, gauging by the seedling growth to assess the levy by reason, all were ordered to contribute grain.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and officials down to commoners, each should be assessed by the acreage of land under cultivation; every autumn, after the harvest is gauged, all should be required to contribute grain.

sentences.zh: 稻麥之鄉，亦同此稅，各納所在，立為義倉。」

translations.literal: In districts of rice and wheat, the same tax applies; each pays where they reside, establishing these as "righteous granaries."
translations.idiomatic: In rice- and wheat-growing regions the same levy should apply; grain would be paid in locally and stored as charitable granaries.

sentences.zh: 太宗從其議。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 以其家貧，齎錢十萬。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor, [the emperor] bestowed one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Because his household was poor, the emperor gave him one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 時尚書左僕射蕭瑀免官，僕射封德彝又卒，太宗謂胄曰：「尚書省天下綱維，百司所稟，若一事有失，天下必有受其弊者。

translations.literal: At that time Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiao Yu was dismissed from office, and Vice Director Feng Deyi also died; Taizong said to Zhou: "The Department of State Affairs is the main rope of all under Heaven, from which the hundred offices receive instruction--if one matter goes wrong, all under Heaven is sure to have those who suffer its harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Director Xiao Yu was dismissed and Vice Director Feng Deyi died, Taizong told Zhou: "The Department of State Affairs is the backbone of the empire; every ministry draws its orders from it. One mistake there, and the whole realm feels the harm.

sentences.zh: 今以令、僕系之於卿，當稱朕所望也。」

translations.literal: Now I entrust the Directors and Vice Directors to you--you should fulfill what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: I now place the directors and vice directors in your charge. You must meet my expectations.

sentences.zh: 胄性明敏，達於從政，處斷明速。

translations.literal: Zhou's character was bright and keen; he was adept at administering government and decisive in judgment, swift in disposal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was quick-witted and skilled at government; his decisions were clear and swift.

sentences.zh: 議者以為左右丞稱職，武德已來，一人而已。

translations.literal: Observers considered that the left and right assistant directors both fulfilled their posts; since Wude, there had been only one such pair.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that both assistant directors were fully equal to their duties--the only such pair since the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 又領諫議大夫，令與魏徵更日供奉。

translations.literal: He also held the post of Supervising Censor and was ordered to attend in audience on alternating days with Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as supervising censor and was ordered to attend the emperor on alternate days with Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，進拜民部尚書，兼檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of the Household and concurrently served as acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to minister of the household and appointed acting left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 先是，右僕射杜如晦專掌選舉，臨終請以選事委胄，由是詔令兼攝吏部尚書，其民部、庶子、諫議並如故。

translations.literal: Before this, Right Vice Director Du Ruhui had been solely in charge of selection and appointment; on his deathbed he requested that selection affairs be entrusted to Zhou. Thereupon an edict ordered him to additionally take charge of Minister of Personnel; his posts as Minister of the Household, Assistant to the Heir, and Supervising Censor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Du Ruhui had previously overseen appointments and examinations alone; on his deathbed he asked that this duty pass to Zhou. An edict accordingly made Zhou acting minister of personnel, while his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 胄雖有干局，而無學術。

translations.literal: Although Zhou had administrative capacity, he lacked scholarly learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had strong executive talent but little formal learning.

sentences.zh: 居吏部，抑文雅而獎法吏，甚為時論所譏。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Personnel, he suppressed the literary and favored legal clerks--this was much ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Personnel he favored legal clerks over men of letters, to the considerable scorn of public opinion.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷吏部尚書，以本官參預朝政，尋進爵為郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was removed as Minister of Personnel; with his existing rank he participated in court deliberations, and soon his noble rank was advanced to Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he relinquished the ministry of personnel but retained his other offices and joined deliberations at court; soon after he was ennobled as duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 五年，太宗將修復洛陽宮，胄上表諫曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year Taizong was about to restore the Luoyang Palace; Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as Taizong prepared to restore the Luoyang palace, Zhou submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 陛下當百王之弊，屬暴隋之後，拯餘燼於塗炭，救遺黎於倒懸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the accumulated abuses of a hundred kings, coming after the tyrannical Sui--snatching embers from smoldering ruins, rescuing survivors from hanging upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherited the accumulated abuses of ages and rose in the wake of the tyrannical Sui, lifting survivors from the ashes and rescuing the people from utter ruin.

sentences.zh: 遠至邇安，率土清謐，大功大德，豈臣之所稱讚。

translations.literal: The distant came and the near were at peace; throughout the land there was clarity and tranquility--such great merit and virtue, how could a subject like me presume to praise them?
translations.idiomatic: The distant submitted and the near found peace; the entire realm knows tranquillity. Such great deeds and virtues are beyond this subject's power to praise.

sentences.zh: 臣誠小人，才識非遠，唯知耳目之近，不達長久之策，敢竭區區之誠，論臣職司之事。

translations.literal: Your servant is truly a petty man; my talent and insight do not reach far--I know only what is before my eyes and do not grasp long-term strategy. I venture to exhaust my trifling sincerity and discuss matters within my official charge.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of small ability with little vision; I see only what lies before me and cannot grasp long-term strategy. Yet I offer my humble sincerity and speak to matters within my office.

sentences.zh: 比見關中、河外，盡置軍團，富室強丁，並從戎旅。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen that in Guanzhong and beyond the Yellow River, army regiments are deployed everywhere; wealthy households' able-bodied men all follow the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have seen military regiments posted throughout Guanzhong and the lands east of the river; able-bodied men from wealthy households have all been pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 重以九成作役，余丁向盡，去京二千里內，先配司農將作。

translations.literal: Added to this is corvee for Jiucheng; the remaining labor quotas are nearly exhausted. Within two thousand li of the capital, men are first assigned to the Directorates of Agriculture and Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this come the levies for Jiucheng Palace; the remaining labor quota is nearly spent. Within two thousand li of the capital, every spare hand has been assigned to the directorates of agriculture and palace construction.

sentences.zh: 假有遺余，勢何足紀？

translations.literal: Even if some remainder were left, what significance would the force be worth recording?
translations.idiomatic: Even if any laborers remain, they amount to nothing worth counting.

sentences.zh: 亂離甫爾，戶口單弱，一人就役，舉家便廢。

translations.literal: Disorder and separation have only just ceased; registered households are thin and weak--when one person goes to corvee, the whole family at once is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has scarcely recovered from war; households are thin and weak. One man taken for corvee, and the whole family is undone.

sentences.zh: 入軍者督其戎仗，從役者責其餱糧，盡室經營，多不能濟。

translations.literal: Those entering the army are pressed for weapons and armor; those on corvee are charged for dry provisions--households exhaust themselves in arrangement, and many cannot manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers must furnish their own arms; corvee workers must supply their own rations. Whole households stretch their resources, and many cannot make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚慮，恐致怨嗟。

translations.literal: In this subject's foolish consideration, I fear this will lead to resentful laments.
translations.idiomatic: I fear, in my limited judgment, that this will breed resentment and complaint.

sentences.zh: 七月已來，霖潦過度，河南、河北，厥田洿下，時豐歲稔，猶未可量。

translations.literal: Since the seventh month floods and excessive rain have occurred; in Henan and Hebei, the fields are low and waterlogged--whether the season will be rich and the year abundant is still not measurable.
translations.idiomatic: Since the seventh month excessive rains have fallen; in Henan and Hebei the low-lying fields are flooded, and whether this year will yield a full harvest remains uncertain.

sentences.zh: 加以軍國所須，皆資府庫，布絹所出，歲過百萬。

translations.literal: Added to this, what army and state require all depends on the treasury; cloth and silk issued exceeds one million each year.
translations.idiomatic: The army and the court depend entirely on the treasury, which disburses more than a million bolts of silk and cloth each year.

sentences.zh: 丁既役盡，賦調不減，費用不止，帑藏其虛。

translations.literal: Since labor quotas are exhausted, taxes and levies are not reduced; expenditures do not stop--the treasury storehouses are empty.
translations.idiomatic: With every able man already conscripted, taxes remain undiminished, expenses unceasing--and the treasury grows bare.

sentences.zh: 且洛陽宮殿，足蔽風雨，數年功畢，亦謂非晚。

translations.literal: Moreover the Luoyang palace is sufficient to shelter from wind and rain; if the work were completed in a few years, that too would not be considered late.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang palace already provides shelter enough; completing renovations over several years would be soon enough.

sentences.zh: 若頓修營，恐傷勞擾。

translations.literal: If restoration and construction are rushed, I fear harm through toil and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: To resume construction now would only inflict further hardship and unrest.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚嘉之，因謂侍臣曰：「戴胄於我無骨肉之親，但以忠直勵行，情深體國，事有機要，無不以聞。

translations.literal: Taizong greatly praised this and then said to his attending ministers: "Dai Zhou has no flesh-and-blood kinship with me, yet through loyalty and rectitude he restrains his conduct; his feeling is deep and his devotion to the state thorough--whenever matters are critical, he withholds nothing from me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong warmly praised the memorial and told his ministers: "Dai Zhou is no kinsman of mine, yet he serves with unwavering loyalty; his devotion to the state runs deep. Whenever a matter of consequence arises, he keeps nothing from me.

sentences.zh: 所進官爵，以酬厥誠耳。」

translations.literal: The offices and noble ranks I have advanced to him are merely to repay his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The offices and titles I have granted him are reward enough for such devotion.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，太宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; Taizong performed mourning rites for him and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year. Taizong mourned him personally and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右僕射，追封道國公，謚曰忠，詔虞世南撰為碑文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo, posthumous title Zhong ("Loyal"); an edict ordered Yu Shinan to compose his epitaph stele.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo with the posthumous name Loyal, and Yu Shinan was commissioned to compose his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 又以胄宅宇弊陋，祭享無所，令有司特為造廟。

translations.literal: Also because Zhou's residence was dilapidated and shabby, with no place for sacrifice and offerings, he ordered the relevant offices specially to build a temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhou's home was too poor and cramped for proper ancestral rites, the emperor ordered officials to build him a temple.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡、魏徵並美胄才用，俱與之親善，及胄卒後，嘗見其游處之地，數為之流涕。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng both admired Zhou's talent and ability and were all close friends with him; after Zhou died, whenever they saw the places where he had walked and lived, they repeatedly wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng both admired Zhou's talent and were close friends with him. After his death, whenever they passed places he had frequented, they wept openly.

sentences.zh: 胄無子，以兄子至德為後。

translations.literal: Zhou had no sons; he made his elder brother's son Zhide his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had no sons and adopted his elder brother's son Zhide as his heir.

sentences.zh: 至德，乾封中累遷西台侍郎、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: Zhide, during the Qianfeng era, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the West Secretariat and granted equal third rank with the East and West Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfeng reign Zhide rose through successive promotions to vice director of the West Secretariat with third-rank parity in both secretariats.

sentences.zh: 尋轉戶部尚書，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of the Household, continuing as before to handle state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to minister of the household while continuing to attend to state affairs.

sentences.zh: 父子十數年間相繼為尚書，預知國政，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son, over a dozen years, successively served as Ministers--participating in advance in state affairs; people of the time considered this an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than a decade father and son held ministerial posts in succession, both shaping national policy--an honor widely noted at the time.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，高宗為飛白書以賜侍臣，賜至德曰「泛洪源，俟舟楫」；

translations.literal: During Xianheng, Gaozong wrote feibai script to bestow on attending ministers; to Zhide he gave "Broaden the flood source, await boats and oars";
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng era, Emperor Gaozong wrote feibai calligraphy for his ministers. To Zhide he gave: "Broaden the great source; await boats and oars";

sentences.zh: 賜郝處俊曰「飛九霄，假六翮」；

translations.literal: to Hao Chujun he gave "Soar through nine heavens, borrow six wing-feathers";
translations.idiomatic: to Hao Chujun: "Soar through the nine heavens; borrow six pinions";

sentences.zh: 賜李敬玄曰「資啟沃，罄丹誠」；

translations.literal: to Li Jingxuan he gave "Assist in nourishment and moistening, exhaust red sincerity";
translations.idiomatic: to Li Jingxuan: "Nourish with counsel; pour out your loyal heart";

sentences.zh: 又賜中書侍郎崔知悌曰「竭忠節，贊皇猷」，其辭皆有興比。

translations.literal: he further gave to Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Zhiti "Exhaust loyal integrity, assist the imperial design"--all the phrases had paralleling metaphors.
translations.idiomatic: and to Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Zhiti: "Exhaust your loyalty; uphold the imperial design." Each phrase carried metaphorical force.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時劉仁軌為左僕射，每遇申訴冤滯者，輒美言許之；

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ren'gui was Left Vice Director; whenever he encountered those appealing grievances of wrongful delay, he would readily speak favorably and promise them relief;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'gui served then as left vice director; whenever petitioners came forward with grievances, he would readily promise them redress;

sentences.zh: 而至德先據理難詰，未嘗與奪，若有理者，密為奏之，終不顯己之斷決，由是時譽歸於仁軌。

translations.literal: But Zhide first examined the reasoning and cross-examined; he never granted or denied on the spot--if the case had merit he secretly memorialized on it, never displaying his own judgment. Hence contemporary reputation went to Ren'gui.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhide would first examine the facts and press hard questions, never ruling on the spot. When a case had merit he memorialized the throne in private, never revealing his own decision. Public credit therefore went to Ren'gui.

sentences.zh: 或以問至德，答曰：「夫慶賞刑罪，人主之權柄，凡為人臣，豈得與人主爭權柄哉！」

translations.literal: Some questioned Zhide about this; he answered: "Reward and punishment, favor and penalty--these are the sovereign's power of command. How can any subject contend with the sovereign for power of command!
translations.idiomatic: When asked about this, Zhide replied: "Rewards and punishments are the sovereign's prerogative. How can a subject compete with his ruler for that power?

sentences.zh: 其慎密如此。

translations.literal: In cautious secrecy he was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his discretion.

sentences.zh: 後高宗知而深嘆美之。

translations.literal: Later Gaozong learned of this and deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong later learned of this, he sighed in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年薨，輟朝三日，使百官以次赴宅哭之，贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng he died; court was suspended three days; officials were sent in sequence to his residence to mourn him; he was posthumously given the honors of Kaifu Yitong San Si and Grand Prefect of Bingzhou; posthumous title Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yifeng 4. Court was suspended for three days, and officials were dispatched in turn to mourn at his home. He was posthumously granted the honors of Kaifu Yitong San Si and appointed grand prefect of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 岑文本，字景仁，南陽棘陽人。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben, styled Jingren, was a man of Jiyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben, courtesy name Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖善方，仕蕭察吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanfang served Xiao Cha as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanfang served as minister of personnel under Xiao Cha.

sentences.zh: 父之象，隋末為邯鄲令，嘗被人所訟，理不得申。

translations.literal: His father Zhixiang, in the late Sui was Magistrate of Handan; he was once sued by someone and could not obtain justice in his case.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixiang served as magistrate of Handan in the late Sui. He was once sued by an accuser and could obtain no justice.

sentences.zh: 文本性沈敏，有姿儀，博考經史，多所貫綜，美談論，善屬文。

translations.literal: Wenben's nature was deep and keen; he had bearing and appearance; he broadly examined the classics and histories and mastered many; he excelled in discourse and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben was thoughtful and quick of mind, handsome in bearing, widely read in the classics and histories, eloquent in debate, and gifted at composition.

sentences.zh: 時年十四，詣司隸稱冤，辭情慨切，召對明辯，眾頗異之。

translations.literal: At the time he was fourteen; he went to the Director of Retainers to plead the injustice; his words and feelings were indignant and earnest. Summoned for audience he was lucid and disputatious; the crowd was quite struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he went to the Director of Retainers to plead his father's case. His words were passionate and precise; summoned for audience, he argued with clear brilliance, and all who heard him were astonished.

sentences.zh: 試令作《蓮花賦》，下筆便成，屬意甚佳，合台莫不歎賞。

translations.literal: They tested him by ordering him to compose 《Lotus Rhapsody》; he put brush to paper and it was finished at once; its meaning and intent were excellent--all in the department none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: They asked him to compose 《Lotus Rhapsody》 on the spot; he finished at the first stroke, and the piece was so fine that everyone present marveled.

sentences.zh: 其父冤雪，由是知名。

translations.literal: His father's injustice was cleared; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: His father's name was cleared, and from that day Wenben was widely known.

sentences.zh: 其後，郡舉秀才，以時亂不應。

translations.literal: Afterward the commandery recommended him as xiucai; because of the disorder of the times he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Later the commandery nominated him as xiucai, but the turmoil of the times kept him from accepting.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑僭號於荊州，召署中書侍郎，專典文翰。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian declared himself emperor at Jingzhou; Wenben was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively handling documents and letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian declared himself emperor at Jingzhou, Wenben was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat to manage all official writings.

sentences.zh: 及河間王孝恭定荊州，軍中將士咸欲大掠，文本進說孝恭曰：「自隋室無道，群雄鼎沸，四海延頸以望真主。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hejian Xiaogong pacified Jingzhou, the army's officers and soldiers all wished to loot on a large scale; Wenben advanced to persuade Xiaogong, saying: "Since the Sui house was without the Way, heroes seethed like a boiling cauldron--throughout the four seas people craned their necks awaiting a true lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiaogong of Hejian pacified Jingzhou, the troops were eager for a general sack. Wenben urged Xiaogong: "Since the Sui lost the Way and warlords rose everywhere, the whole realm has longed for a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今蕭氏君臣、江陵父老，決計歸降者，實望去危就安耳。

translations.literal: Now the lord and ministers of the Xiao house and the elders of Jiangling who resolved to surrender did so in fact to leave danger and seek safety.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao court and the elders of Jiangling have decided to submit because they wish to escape danger and find safety--nothing more.

sentences.zh: 王必欲縱兵虜掠，誠非鄙州來蘇之意，亦恐江、嶺以南，向化之心沮矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness must unleash troops to plunder captives, it truly is not this humble province's intent of coming back to life, and I also fear that south of the Jiang and Ling ranges, hearts inclined toward civilization will be dampened.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness insists on letting the army sack and plunder, that is hardly what this province hoped for when it welcomed deliverance—and I fear it will crush the will to submit among all who lie south of the Yangzi and the Ling ranges.

sentences.zh: 孝恭稱善，遂止之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong praised this as good and thereupon stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong approved the advice and halted the planned sack.

sentences.zh: 署文本荊州別駕。

translations.literal: He appointed Wenben Vice Prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wenben vice prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝恭進擊輔公祏，召典軍書，復署行台考功郎中。

translations.literal: When Xiaogong advanced to attack Fu Gongshi, he summoned Wenben to manage military documents and again appointed him Bureau Director of Merit Assessment in the mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogong marched against Fu Gongshi, he summoned Wenben to handle military correspondence and also named him director of merit assessment in the field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，除秘書郎，兼直中書省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Wenben was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library and concurrently served on duty in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, he was made a secretary in the Palace Library and assigned concurrent duty in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遇太宗行藉田之禮，文本上《藉田頌》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong performed the ritual plowing ceremony, Wenben presented 《Hymn on the Ploughing Field》.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong performed the ceremonial ploughing of the sacred field, Wenben submitted 《Hymn on the Ploughing Field》.

sentences.zh: 及元日臨軒宴百僚，文本復上《三元頌》，其辭甚美。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, when the emperor held a feast for the hundred officials before the palace hall, Wenben again presented 《Hymn on the Three Beginnings》, and its language was exceedingly fine.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when the emperor feasted the hundred officials in the palace hall, Wenben again presented 《Hymn on the Three Beginnings》, and the piece was beautifully wrought.

sentences.zh: 文本才名既著，李靖復稱薦之，擢拜中書舍人，漸蒙親顧。

translations.literal: Once Wenben's talent and fame were well established, Li Jing again praised and recommended him; he was promoted and appointed Secretariat Drafter, and gradually received the emperor's personal regard.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wenben's literary reputation was firmly established. Li Jing recommended him again, and he was promoted to secretariat drafter, gradually winning the emperor's personal favor.

sentences.zh: 初，武德中詔誥及軍國大事，文皆出於顏師古。

translations.literal: Initially, during the Wude era, edicts, proclamations, and documents on military and state affairs all came from Yan Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: At first, throughout the Wude era, all edicts, proclamations, and papers on military and state affairs had been drafted by Yan Shigu.

sentences.zh: 至是，文本所草詔誥。

translations.literal: From this time forward, the edicts and proclamations Wenben drafted.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, edicts and proclamations were Wenben's to draft.

sentences.zh: 或眾務繁湊，即命書僮六七人隨口並寫，須臾悉成，亦殆盡其妙。

translations.literal: Sometimes when many duties piled up, he would order six or seven copy boys to write simultaneously as he dictated orally; in a moment all would be finished, nearly exhausting the full measure of his skill.
translations.idiomatic: When business piled up, he would summon six or seven copyists and dictate several documents at once; in no time all were finished—a virtuosity that seemed to leave nothing of his art unused.

sentences.zh: 時中書侍郎顏師古以譴免職，頃之，溫彥博奏曰：「師古諳練時事，長於文法，時無及者，冀蒙復用。」

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Yan Shigu was dismissed from office on account of censure. Shortly afterward, Wen Yanbo memorialized: "Shigu is thoroughly versed in current affairs and excels in literary form; there is no one of the age who equals him. I hope he may be restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: About then Vice Director Yan Shigu was dismissed after a reprimand. Before long Wen Yanbo memorialized: "Shigu knows the affairs of the day inside out and excels at formal prose; no one alive matches him. I hope he may be restored to service.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「我自舉一人，公勿憂也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "I myself will recommend one man. Sir, do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "I will recommend someone myself. Do not trouble yourself over it.

sentences.zh: 於是以文本為中書侍郎，專典機密。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenben was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively handling confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wenben was made vice director of the Secretariat with sole charge of confidential business.

sentences.zh: 又先與令狐德棻撰《周史》，其史論多出於文本。

translations.literal: He had earlier joined Linghu Defen in compiling 《History of Zhou》, and most of its historical assessments came from Wenben.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier worked with Linghu Defen on 《History of Zhou》, and most of its historical judgments were Wenben's.

sentences.zh: 至十年史成，封江陵縣子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the history was completed, and he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was finished in the tenth year, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從至洛陽宮，會谷、洛泛溢，文本上封事曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he accompanied the emperor to Luoyang Palace. When the Gu and Luo rivers overflowed, Wenben submitted a sealed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he accompanied the emperor to the Luoyang palace. When the Gu and Luo rivers burst their banks, Wenben submitted a sealed memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞創撥亂之業，其功既難；

translations.literal: I have heard that founding an enterprise amid chaos is already a difficult achievement;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to build an empire out of chaos is hard enough;

sentences.zh: 守已成之基，其道不易。

translations.literal: to preserve a foundation already established, its Way is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: to preserve what has already been won is no less difficult.

sentences.zh: 故居安思危，所以定其業也；

translations.literal: Therefore, in dwelling at ease to think of peril is how one settles one's enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that in peace one must think of peril—that is how a realm is made secure;

sentences.zh: 有始有卒，所以隆其基也。

translations.literal: to have a beginning and a completion is how one exalts one's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: and that a task begun must be carried through to the end—that is how its foundation is raised high.

sentences.zh: 今雖億兆乂安，方隅寧謐，既承喪亂之後，又接凋弊之餘，戶口減損尚多，田疇墾闢猶少。

translations.literal: Though now the myriad masses are governed in peace and the regions are tranquil and still, having succeeded upon the heels of turmoil and slaughter and inheriting the aftermath of decline and exhaustion, the population yet diminished is still considerable and arable fields opened for cultivation remain few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is now at peace and the provinces quiet, we have come out of slaughter and inherit a land still wasted and exhausted. The population remains greatly reduced, and fields newly opened to the plough are still too few.

sentences.zh: 覆燾之恩著矣，而瘡痍未復；

translations.literal: The sheltering warmth of your grace is manifest, yet the wounds of war are not yet healed;
translations.idiomatic: Your sheltering grace is plain to see, yet the scars of war have not healed;

sentences.zh: 德教之風被矣，而資產屢空。

translations.literal: The wind of virtue and instruction has spread, yet households' assets are repeatedly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: the wind of virtue and instruction has reached everywhere, yet many households still have nothing to their name.

sentences.zh: 是以古人譬之種樹，年祀綿遠，則枝葉扶疏；

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients compared it to planting a tree: when years extend far, then branches and leaves grow luxuriant;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients compared this to planting a tree: given many years, its branches and leaves grow thick;

sentences.zh: 若種之日淺，根本未固，雖壅之以黑墳，暖之以春日，一人搖之，必致枯槁。

translations.literal: If the day of planting is shallow and the root and trunk are not yet firm, though one heaps black soil upon it and warms it with spring sunlight, a single person shaking it will necessarily bring withering and death.
translations.idiomatic: but if it was planted only yesterday and its roots are not yet firm, then though you heap rich black earth around it and warm it with spring sun, one man's shake will still wither it to death.

sentences.zh: 今之百姓，頗類於此。

translations.literal: The people of today quite resemble this.
translations.idiomatic: The common people today are much like that tree.

sentences.zh: 常加含養，則日就滋息；

translations.literal: If constantly given nurture and care, they daily approach increase and prosperity;
translations.idiomatic: Nurture them steadily and they will daily grow stronger;

sentences.zh: 暫有征役，則隨而凋耗。

translations.literal: If there is brief conscript labor or corvée, they straightaway decline and waste away.
translations.idiomatic: impose corvée or conscription even briefly and they at once waste away.

sentences.zh: 凋耗既甚，則人不卿生；

translations.literal: Once decline and wastage are extreme, the people cannot bear to live;
translations.idiomatic: When waste becomes extreme, the people cannot bear to live;

sentences.zh: 人不卿生，則怨氣充塞；

translations.literal: When the people cannot bear to live, then resentful qi fills the realm;
translations.idiomatic: when the people cannot bear to live, resentment fills the land;

sentences.zh: 怨氣充塞，則離叛之心生矣。

translations.literal: When resentful qi fills the realm, then hearts of separation and rebellion arise.
