translations.idiomatic: when resentment fills the land, hearts turn to separation and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 故帝舜曰：「可愛非君，可畏非人。」

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Shun said: "What is to be loved is not the ruler; what is to be feared is not the people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun therefore said, "What is to be loved is not the ruler; what is to be feared is not the people.

sentences.zh: 孔安國曰：「人以君為命，故可愛；

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said: "People take the ruler as their life, therefore he can be loved;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo explained: "The people look to the ruler for their very lives, and so he may be loved;

sentences.zh: 君失道，人叛之，故可畏。」

translations.literal: When the ruler loses the Way and people rebel against him, therefore he can be feared.
translations.idiomatic: but when the ruler loses the Way and the people turn against him, then he has reason to fear.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「君猶舟也，人猶水也；

translations.literal: Confucius said: "The ruler is like a boat, the people like water;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The ruler is like a boat and the people like water;

sentences.zh: 水所以載舟，亦所以覆舟。」

translations.literal: Water is what carries the boat, and also what capsizes it.
translations.idiomatic: water carries the boat, and water also capsizes it.

sentences.zh: 是以古之哲王，雖休勿休，日慎一日者，良為此也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity, though at rest would not rest, and grew more cautious day by day—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage kings of old, though at rest would not rest and grew more careful day by day.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下覽古今之事，察安危之機，上以社稷為重，下以億兆為念。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty should review affairs past and present, discern the pivot of safety and peril, above take the altars of soil and grain as weighty, below take the myriad masses to heart.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to survey affairs past and present, weigh the turning points of safety and peril, hold the altars of state above all else, and keep the myriad people close in mind.

sentences.zh: 明選舉，慎賞罰，進賢才，退不肖。

translations.literal: Make clear appointments, be cautious in rewards and punishments, advance the worthy and talented, dismiss the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Choose officials wisely, weigh rewards and punishments carefully, promote the worthy, and remove the unfit.

sentences.zh: 聞過即改，從諫如流。

translations.literal: Hear of faults and immediately reform; follow remonstrance as water follows its course.
translations.idiomatic: Amend faults the moment you hear of them, and follow remonstrance as a stream follows its bed.

sentences.zh: 為善在於不疑，出令期於必信。

translations.literal: Doing good lies in not doubting; issuing orders should aim at certain trust.
translations.idiomatic: Good government requires steadfast resolve; edicts must be issued only when they can be trusted to endure.

sentences.zh: 頤神養性，省畋游之娛；

translations.literal: Nourish the spirit and cultivate the nature; reduce the pleasure of hunting excursions;
translations.idiomatic: Nourish body and mind, and cut back on the pleasures of the hunt;

sentences.zh: 去奢從儉，減工役之費。

translations.literal: Cast off extravagance and follow frugality; reduce the expense of labor projects.
translations.idiomatic: cast off extravagance for thrift, and reduce the cost of public works.

sentences.zh: 務靜方內而不求闢土；

translations.literal: Dedicate yourself to tranquility within the realm and do not seek to open new territory;
translations.idiomatic: Keep the realm at peace within and do not seek to expand its borders;

sentences.zh: 載橐弓矢而無忘武備。

translations.literal: Bear bow and arrows in the quiver and do not forget military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: yet keep bow and quiver at hand and never forget readiness for war.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，雖為國之常道，陛下之所常行，臣之愚心，唯願陛下思之而不倦，行之而不怠。

translations.literal: All these several points, though they are the constant Way of governing the state and what Your Majesty constantly practices, in this one's foolish heart I only wish that Your Majesty would ponder them without weariness and carry them out without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: All these are the ordinary duties of rule, and Your Majesty already practices them; yet in my foolish heart I can only ask that you ponder them without tiring and carry them out without slackening.

sentences.zh: 則至道之美，與三、五比隆；

translations.literal: Then the beauty of the utmost Way would vie in eminence with the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Then the splendor of the highest Way would stand beside the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 億載之祚，隨天地長久。

translations.literal: The tenure of myriad ages would endure as long as Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: and the throne would endure for myriad ages, lasting as long as Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 雖使桑谷為妖，龍蛇作孽，雉雊於鼎耳，石言於晉地，猶當轉禍為福，變咎為祥。

translations.literal: Even were mulberry and grain to become portents of ill omen, dragons and serpents to work calamities, pheasants to crow at tripod ears, and stones to speak in Jin territory, you would still turn misfortune into fortune and transform blame into auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Even if mulberry and grain turned monstrous, dragons and serpents wrought havoc, pheasants cried from tripod ears, and stones spoke in the land of Jin, you would still turn misfortune to blessing and transform ill omens into good.

sentences.zh: 況水雨之患，陰陽常理，豈可謂之天譴而系聖心哉？

translations.literal: How much more so when the calamity is merely flooding rain, the regular principle of yin and yang—how can this be called heaven's punishment and tied to the sagely heart?
translations.idiomatic: How much less, then, should flooding rain—an ordinary turn of yin and yang—be called heaven's rebuke and allowed to weigh upon Your Majesty's heart?

sentences.zh: 臣聞古人有言：「農夫勞而君子養焉，愚者言而智者擇焉。」

translations.literal: I have heard the ancients say: "The farmer labors and the gentleman is nourished thereby; the foolish speak and the wise choose among their words.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "The farmer toils and the gentleman is nourished; the fool speaks and the wise man chooses.

sentences.zh: 輒陳狂瞽，伏待斧鉞。

translations.literal: I presumptuously offer these rash and blind words and humbly await the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: I have presumptuously offered these rash and blind words and humbly await your judgment.

sentences.zh: 是時魏王泰寵冠諸王，盛修第宅，文本以為侈不可長，上疏盛陳節儉之義，言泰宜有抑損，太宗並嘉之，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Wei Tai's favor surpassed all other princes, and he lavishly built mansions and residences. Wenben considered that extravagance must not be allowed to grow; he submitted a memorial vigorously expounding the meaning of thrift, saying that Tai should exercise restraint and reduction. Emperor Taizong praised both points and granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Tai of Wei enjoyed favor above all other princes and built mansions on a lavish scale. Wenben held that extravagance must not be indulged; he memorialized at length on thrift and urged that Tai should show restraint. Emperor Taizong approved both points and granted him three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Glory with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Glory with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 文本自以出自書生，每懷捴損。

translations.literal: Wenben, considering himself to come from the ranks of scholar-literati, always cherished self-restraint and modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben, knowing himself to be a man of the brush rather than the sword, always practiced self-restraint and modesty.

sentences.zh: 平生故人，雖微賤必與之抗禮。

translations.literal: Old friends of his whole life, even if lowly in station, he invariably treated as equals in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends from his earlier days, however humble, he always greeted as equals.

sentences.zh: 居處卑陋，室無茵褥帷帳之飾。

translations.literal: His dwelling was humble and plain; his rooms had none of the adornments of mats, cushions, curtains, or canopies.
translations.idiomatic: His home was plain and lowly, with none of the mats, cushions, curtains, or hangings that mark a grand house.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞，撫弟侄恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: He was known for filial devotion to his mother and treated younger brothers and nephews with deep kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother and treated his younger brothers and nephews with deep affection and duty.

sentences.zh: 太宗每言其「弘厚忠謹，吾親之信之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong often said of him: "Magnanimous, sincere, loyal, and careful—I trust him as one trusts kin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong often said of him, "Magnanimous, loyal, and careful—I trust him as I would my own kin.

sentences.zh: 是時，新立晉王為皇太子，名士多兼領宮官，太宗欲令文本兼攝。

translations.literal: At this time, the Prince of Jin had newly been established as Crown Prince; eminent men mostly held concurrent posts as palace officials, and Emperor Taizong wished to have Wenben serve concurrently as well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jin had just been made crown prince. Many eminent men held concurrent posts in the Eastern Palace, and Emperor Taizong wished Wenben to serve there as well.

sentences.zh: 文本再拜曰：「臣以庸才，久逾涯分，守此一職，猶懼滿盈，豈宜更忝春坊，以速時謗。

translations.literal: Wenben bowed twice and said: "Your subject, with mediocre talent, has long exceeded the bounds of his worth. To hold this one office—I still fear I am brimful. How could I properly also assume a post in the Eastern Palace and thereby invite the slanders of the age?
translations.idiomatic: Wenben bowed twice and said, "Your subject is a man of modest talent who has long outstripped his deserts. Even this one office fills me with fear of excess. How could I also take a post in the Eastern Palace and invite the censure of the age?

sentences.zh: 臣請一心以事陛下，不願更希東宮恩澤。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks only to serve Your Majesty with undivided heart and does not wish further to seek the grace of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to serve Your Majesty with an undivided heart and do not wish to seek further favor from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 仍令五日一參東宮，皇太子執賓友之禮，與之答拜。

translations.literal: He still ordered Wenben to attend the Eastern Palace once every five days; the Crown Prince performed the courtesy due to a guest and friend, exchanging bows with him in reply.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Wenben to attend the Eastern Palace once every five days; the crown prince received him with the courtesy due a guest and friend, exchanging bows in reply.

sentences.zh: 其見待如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書令，歸家有憂色，其母怪而問之，文本曰：「非勳非舊，濫荷寵榮，責重位高，所以憂懼。」

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief Director of the Secretariat. Returning home with a troubled expression, his mother wondered and asked him. Wenben said: "Without merit or longstanding service, I have undeservedly received favor and glory; responsibility is heavy and rank is high—this is why I am anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed chief director of the Secretariat. He returned home wearing a troubled look, and his mother, puzzled, asked why. Wenben said, "I have no merit and no long service behind me, yet I have been showered with favor and rank. The burden is heavy and the position is high—that is why I am afraid.

sentences.zh: 親賓有來慶賀，輒曰：「今受吊，不受賀也。」

translations.literal: When relatives and guests came to offer congratulations, he would say: "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives and friends came to congratulate him, he would say, "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations.

sentences.zh: 又有勸其營產業者，文本嘆曰：「南方一布衣，徒步入關，疇昔之望，不過秘書郎、一縣令耳。

translations.literal: There were also those who urged him to build up estates and property. Wenben sighed and said: "I was a plain-clothed man of the south who entered the pass on foot. My hopes in former days extended no further than a secretary in the Palace Library and a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to build up property and estates. Wenben sighed and said, "I was a plain-clothed man from the south who entered the pass on foot. In those days I hoped for nothing more than a post as palace secretary or county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 而無汗馬之勞，徒以文墨致位中書令，斯亦極矣。

translations.literal: Without labor of horse and sword, I have reached the Chief Directorship of the Secretariat by literary ink alone—this already is the pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: Without a single hour's labor in the saddle, I have reached the chief directorship by ink alone—that is already the summit.

sentences.zh: 荷俸祿之重，為懼已多，何得更言產業乎？」

translations.literal: To bear the weight of salary and stipends is already more than enough cause for fear—how can I speak further of estates and property?
translations.idiomatic: The weight of my salary already gives me more than enough to fear—how could I speak of acquiring estates?

sentences.zh: 言者嘆息而退。

translations.literal: Those who had spoken sighed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had spoken sighed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文本既久在樞揆，當涂任事，賞錫稠疊，凡有財物出入，皆委季弟文昭，一無所問。

translations.literal: Wenben having long served at the pivot of government, when he held power and handled affairs, rewards and gifts piled thick. All disbursements and receipts of goods and wealth he entrusted to his youngest brother Wenzhao, questioning nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben had long stood at the pivot of power. While he held office, rewards and gifts piled up; every disbursement and receipt he entrusted to his youngest brother Wenzhao without asking a single question.

sentences.zh: 文昭時任校書郎，多與時人遊款，太宗聞而不悅，嘗從容謂文本曰：「卿弟過多交結，恐累卿，朕將出之為外官，如何？」

translations.literal: Wenzhao at the time served as collator; he associated freely with many men of the age. Emperor Taizong heard of this and was displeased. He once spoke at ease to Wenben: "Your younger brother has too many social connections—I fear this may implicate you. I intend to send him out as an official elsewhere. What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was then a collating clerk and kept company with many men of the day. Emperor Taizong heard of this and was displeased. He once said casually to Wenben, "Your brother keeps too many acquaintances—I fear it may harm you. I mean to send him out to a post elsewhere. What say you?

sentences.zh: 文本泣曰：「臣弟少孤，老母特所鍾念，不欲信宿離於左右。

translations.literal: Wenben wept and said: "Your subject's younger brother lost his father young; our elderly mother especially dotes on him and cannot bear to be parted from him even overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben wept and said, "My brother lost his father young. Our old mother dotes on him above all and cannot bear to be parted from him even for a night.

sentences.zh: 若今外出，母必憂悴，儻無此弟，亦無老母也。」

translations.literal: If he is sent out now, our mother will surely fall into grief and wasting. If I did not have this brother, I would have no elderly mother either.
translations.idiomatic: If he is sent away now, she will surely waste away with grief. Without this brother, I would have no mother left either.

sentences.zh: 歔欷嗚咽，太宗愍其意而止。

translations.literal: Sniffling and sobbing, he wept aloud. Emperor Taizong took pity on his meaning and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and wept aloud. Emperor Taizong was moved by his plea and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 唯召見文昭，嚴加誡約，亦卒無愆過。

translations.literal: He only summoned Wenzhao and strictly admonished and restrained him; in the end there were no faults or lapses.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wenzhao instead and gave him a stern warning; in the end Wenzhao committed no further fault.

sentences.zh: 及將伐遼，凡所籌度，一皆委之。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Liaodong was about to begin, all planning and calculations were entirely entrusted to Wenben.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Liaodong was about to begin, every plan and calculation was entrusted to Wenben alone.

sentences.zh: 文本受委既深，神情頓竭，言辭舉措，頗異平常。

translations.literal: Wenben, having received so deep a trust, suddenly exhausted his spirit and energy; his words, deportment, and conduct were quite unlike the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Burdened with so heavy a trust, Wenben's spirit suddenly gave way; his speech and bearing were markedly unlike his usual self.

sentences.zh: 太宗見而憂之，謂左右曰：「文本今與我同行，恐不與我同返。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong saw this and was troubled. He said to those around him: "Wenben is traveling with me now—I fear he will not return with me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong saw this and was troubled. He said to those around him, "Wenben is marching with me now—I fear he will not march back with me.

sentences.zh: 及至幽州，遇暴疾，太宗親自臨視，撫之流涕。

translations.literal: When they reached Youzhou, Wenben was stricken with a sudden acute illness. Emperor Taizong personally came to look in on him, stroking him and shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Youzhou, Wenben was stricken with a sudden grave illness. Emperor Taizong came in person to his bedside, stroked him, and wept.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 其夕，太宗聞嚴鼓之聲，曰：「文本殞逝，情深惻怛。

translations.literal: That evening, Emperor Taizong heard the night-watch drums and said: "Wenben has fallen and passed—my grief is deep and poignant.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, when Emperor Taizong heard the night-watch drums, he said, "Wenben has died, and my grief cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 今宵夜警，所不忍聞。」

translations.literal: Tonight's midnight alarms—I cannot bear to hear them.
translations.idiomatic: Tonight's midnight alarms are more than I can bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 命停之。

translations.literal: He ordered them stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them stopped.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、廣州都督，謚曰憲，賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the post of Palace Attendant and Area Commander of Guangzhou, given the posthumous name Xian, granted the Eastern Garden secret burial rites, and interred with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and area commander of Guangzhou, given the posthumous name Xian, granted the Eastern Garden burial regalia, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 有集六十捲行於代。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in sixty scroll volumes that circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, in sixty scroll volumes, circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 文本兄文叔。

translations.literal: Wenben's elder brother Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's elder brother was Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 文叔子長倩，少為文本所鞠，同於己子。

translations.literal: Wenshu's son Changqian, from youth was raised by Wenben as if he were his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu's son Changqian was raised from boyhood by Wenben as though he were his own child.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，累轉兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: During the Yongchun era, he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of War and Concurrent Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun era he rose through successive posts to vice minister of war and concurrent grand councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，自夏官尚書遷內史，知夏官事，俄拜文昌右相，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era, he moved from Minister of the Summer Office to Grand Secretary, retaining charge of Summer Office affairs; soon he was appointed Right Chancellor of the Literary Flourishing Hall and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chuigong era he moved from minister of the Summer Office to grand secretary while retaining charge of Summer Office affairs; soon he was made right chancellor of the Literary Flourishing Hall and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 則天初革命，尤好符瑞，長倩懼罪，頗有陳奏，又上疏請改皇嗣姓為武氏，以為周室儲貳，則天許之，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu first changed the dynasty, she especially favored portents and omens. Changqian, fearing guilt, made several memorial submissions, and also submitted a memorial requesting that the surname of the Crown Prince be changed to the Wu clan, making him heir apparent of the Zhou house. Empress Wu granted this, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu first changed the dynasty she was especially fond of portents and omens. Changqian, fearing blame, memorialized repeatedly and also asked that the crown prince's surname be changed to Wu so that he might serve as heir of the Zhou house. Empress Wu granted this and gave him a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，加特進、輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, he was given the additional titles of Senior Grand Master and Grand General Assisting the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou he was given the additional titles Senior Grand Master and Grand General Assisting the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，鳳閣舍人張嘉福與洛州人王慶之等列名上表，請立武承嗣為皇太子。

translations.literal: That year, Phoenix Pavilion Drafting Official Zhang Jiafu and Wang Qingzhi of Luozhou and others jointly submitted a memorial requesting that Wu Chengsi be established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That year Phoenix Pavilion drafting official Zhang Jiafu, Wang Qingzhi of Luozhou, and others jointly submitted a memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 長倩以皇嗣在東宮，不可更立承嗣，與地官尚書格輔元竟不署名，仍奏請切責上書者。

translations.literal: Changqian, considering that the Crown Prince was already established in the Eastern Palace and Chengsi could not be set up in his place, together with Minister of the Earth Office Ge Fuyuan ultimately refused to sign. They also memorialized requesting stern censure of those who had submitted the petition.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian held that with the crown prince already established in the Eastern Palace, Chengsi could not be set up in his stead. He and Minister of the Earth Office Ge Fuyuan refused to sign the memorial and submitted a request for stern punishment of those who had petitioned.

sentences.zh: 由是大忤諸武意，乃斥令西征吐蕃，充武威道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: By this he greatly offended the will of the Wu clan, and was expelled and ordered west to campaign against Tibet, serving as Grand General of the March on the Weiwu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: This greatly offended the Wu clan. He was sent west to campaign against Tibet as grand general of the march on the Weiwu circuit.

sentences.zh: 中路召還，下制獄，被誅，仍發掘其父祖墳墓。

translations.literal: Midway he was recalled, thrown into the imperial prison, executed, and his father's and grandfather's tombs were still disinterred.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he was recalled, thrown into the imperial prison, and executed; his father's and grandfather's graves were then dug up as well.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣又脅迫長倩子靈源，令誣納言歐陽通及格輔元等數十人，皆陷以同反之罪，並誅死。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen also coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan, forcing him to falsely accuse Chief Minister Ouyang Tong, Ge Fuyuan, and several dozen others—all were trapped on charges of conspiracy to rebel and were put to death together.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen also coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan into falsely accusing Chief Minister Ouyang Tong, Ge Fuyuan, and several dozen others. All were convicted of conspiracy to rebel and executed.

sentences.zh: 長倩子羲，長安中為廣武令，有能名。

translations.literal: Changqian's son Xi served as magistrate of Guangwu during the Chang'an era and was known for his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian's son Xi served as magistrate of Guangwu during the Chang'an era and was known for his ability.

sentences.zh: 則天嘗令宰相各舉堪為員外郎者，鳳閣侍郎韋嗣立薦羲，且奏曰：「恨其從父長倩犯逆為累。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu once ordered each chancellor to recommend someone fit to serve as a vice director; Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Wei Sili recommended Xi and memorialized, saying: "I regret that his paternal uncle Changqian's conviction for treason is a burden upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once ordered each chancellor to recommend someone fit for a vice directorship. Wei Sili, vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, recommended Xi but added in his memorial, "My regret is that his paternal uncle Changqian was condemned for treason—a stain that weighs against him.

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「苟有材幹，何恨微累？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: "If he has talent and capacity, why regret a slight burden?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "If he has talent and ability, what matter a minor blemish?

sentences.zh: 遂拜天官員外郎。

translations.literal: Xi was thereupon appointed Vice Director of the Celestial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was thereupon appointed vice director of the Celestial Office.

sentences.zh: 由是緣坐近親，相次入省，登封令劉守悌為司門員外郎，渭南令裴惓為地官員外郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon, through association as close kin, they entered the Secretariat in succession: Magistrate of Dengfeng Liu Shouti became Vice Director of the Gate Office, and Magistrate of Weinan Pei Min became Vice Director of the Earth Office.
translations.idiomatic: Through their connection as close associates, they too entered the Secretariat in turn: Liu Shouti, magistrate of Dengfeng, became vice director of the Gate Office, and Pei Min, magistrate of Weinan, became vice director of the Earth Office.

sentences.zh: 先是，羲為金壇令，守悌及惓稱為清德。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xi had been magistrate of Jintan, Shouti and Min had praised him for pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xi had served as magistrate of Jintan, Shouti and Min had praised his upright character.

sentences.zh: 羲以文吏著名，俱為巡察使所薦，皆授畿縣令，又同為尚書郎，悉有美譽。

translations.literal: Xi was famed as a literate administrator; all three were recommended by inspection commissioners, were all appointed magistrates of capital-area counties, later served together as Masters of Writing, and all enjoyed fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was known as an accomplished literary official. All three were recommended by inspection commissioners and appointed magistrates in the capital region; later they served together as masters of writing, and each earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 守悌後至陝州刺史，惓至杭州刺史。

translations.literal: Shouti later rose to Prefect of Shaan Province; Min rose to Prefect of Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouti later became prefect of Shaan Province, and Min became prefect of Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 羲，神龍初為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xi, at the beginning of the Shenlong era, served as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Xi served as drafting secretary of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時武三思用事，侍中敬暉欲上表請削諸武之為王者，募為疏者。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi held power; Palace Attendant Jing Hui wished to submit a memorial requesting that the Wu clan members who had been made kings be stripped of their titles, and sought someone to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Sansi held sway at court. Palace Attendant Jing Hui wished to submit a memorial asking that the Wu princes be stripped of their royal titles, and sought someone to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 眾畏三思，皆辭托不敢為之，羲便操筆，辭甚切直。

translations.literal: The multitude feared Sansi; all declined on pretexts and dared not write it. Xi took up the brush at once, and his language was very forceful and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared Sansi and begged off; none dared to write it. Xi took up the brush himself, and his language was sharp and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 由是忤三思意，轉秘書少監，再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: By this he offended Sansi's intent; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and later promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: This offended Sansi. Xi was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and later promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎崔湜、太常少卿鄭愔、大理少卿李元恭分掌選事，皆以贓貨聞，羲最守正，時議美之。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Shi, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yin, and Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Li Yuangong divided charge of selection affairs; all were known for bribery, while Xi was most upright—contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Shi, vice minister of personnel; Zheng Yin, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Li Yuangong, vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, shared control of appointments. All were notorious for taking bribes, but Xi held most firmly to rectitude, and public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫、右散騎常侍、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles Silver Purple-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Right Regular Attendant, and Third Rank, Participating with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional titles silver purple-gleam grand master of splendid happiness, right regular attendant, and third rank, participating with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，出為陝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Xi was sent out as Prefect of Shaan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Xi was sent out to serve as prefect of Shaan Province.

sentences.zh: 復歷刑部、戶部二尚書，門下三品，監修國史，刪定格令，仍修《氏族錄》。

translations.literal: He again served in succession as Minister of Punishments and Minister of Revenue, held third rank in the Chancellery, directed compilation of the national history, revised codes and statutes, and also compiled the 《Genealogical Records》.
translations.idiomatic: He again served in turn as minister of punishments and minister of revenue, held third rank in the Chancellery, directed compilation of the national history, revised the codes and statutes, and also worked on the 《Genealogical Records》.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗時，侍御史冉祖雍誣奏睿宗及太平公主與節愍太子連謀，請加推究，羲與中書侍郎蕭至忠密申保護。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the reign of Emperor Zhongzong, Investigating Censor Ran Zuyong falsely memorialized that Emperor Ruizong and Princess Taiping had conspired with Crown Prince Jiemin, requesting further investigation. Xi and Vice Minister of the Secretariat Xiao Zhizhong secretly pleaded in their defense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Emperor Zhongzong's reign, investigating censor Ran Zuyong falsely accused Emperor Ruizong and Princess Taiping of plotting with Crown Prince Jiemin and asked that the matter be pursued to the end. Xi and vice minister of the Secretariat Xiao Zhizhong secretly intervened on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 及羲監修《中宗實錄》，自書其事，睿宗覽而大加賞嘆，賜物三百段、良馬一匹，仍下制書褒美之。

translations.literal: When Xi directed compilation of the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Zhongzong》 and himself recorded this affair, Emperor Ruizong read it and greatly praised and sighed in admiration, granting three hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse, and also issuing an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi, as director of the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Zhongzong》, recorded the affair himself, Emperor Ruizong read the account and was deeply moved. He rewarded Xi with three hundred bolts of goods and a fine horse, and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 時羲兄獻為國子司業，弟翔為陝州刺史，休為商州刺史，從族兄弟子侄，因羲引用登清要者數十人。

translations.literal: At the time Xi's elder brother Xian was Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers Xiang was Prefect of Shaan Province and Xiu was Prefect of Shang Prefecture; and several dozen clansmen, brothers, sons, and nephews reached prestigious posts through Xi's patronage.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xi's elder brother Xian was vice director of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers Xiang and Xiu were prefects of Shaan and Shang respectively; and several dozen kinsmen—brothers, sons, and nephews—won prestigious posts through Xi's patronage.

sentences.zh: 羲嘆曰：「物極則返，可以懼矣！」

translations.literal: Xi sighed and said: "When things reach their extreme they turn back—one may take alarm from this!
translations.idiomatic: Xi sighed and said, "When things reach their height they turn—there is reason to fear!

sentences.zh: 然竟不能有所抑退。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he could not restrain or send any of them away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he could not bring himself to restrain or dismiss any of them.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Chief Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to chief attendant.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，坐預太平公主謀逆伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian, for participation in Princess Taiping's plot of treason he was executed, and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian he was executed for taking part in Princess Taiping's conspiracy, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 格輔元者，汴州浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Ge Fuyuan was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Fuyuan was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯父德仁，隋剡縣丞，與同郡人齊王文學王孝逸、文林郎繁師玄、羅川郡戶曹靖君亮、司隸從事鄭祖咸、宣城縣長鄭師善、王世充中書舍人李行簡、處士盧協等八人，以辭學擅名，當時號為「陳留八俊」。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Deren had been Assistant Magistrate of Yan County under Sui; together with eight men of the same commandery famed for literary learning—Literary Instructor to Prince of Qi Wang Xiaoyi, Gentleman of the Forest of Letters Fan Shixuan, Registrar of Households in Luochuan Commandery Jing Junliang, Clerk of the Inspectorate Zheng Zuxian, District Magistrate of Xuancheng Zheng Shishan, Drafting Secretary to Wang Shichong Li Xingjian, and Recluse Lu Xie—they were called at the time the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Deren had served Sui as assistant magistrate of Yan County. Together with seven others from the same commandery who were famed for literary accomplishment—Wang Xiaoyi, literary instructor to the Prince of Qi; Fan Shixuan, gentleman of the Forest of Letters; Jing Junliang, registrar of households in Luochuan Commandery; Zheng Zuxian, clerk of the inspectorate; Zheng Shishan, district magistrate of Xuancheng; Li Xingjian, drafting secretary to Wang Shichong; and the recluse Lu Xie—they were known in their day as the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."

sentences.zh: 輔元弱冠舉明經，歷遷御史大夫、地官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Fuyuan, upon coming of age, passed the Mingjing examination; he rose through successive posts to Censor-in-Chief, Minister of the Earth Office, and Grand Councillor of the Phoenix Pavilion-Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan passed the Mingjing examination at coming of age and rose through successive posts to censor-in-chief, minister of the Earth Office, and grand councillor of the Phoenix Pavilion-Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 初，張嘉福等請立武承嗣也，則天以問輔元，固稱不可，遂為承嗣所譖而死，海內冤之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Jiafu and others requested that Wu Chengsi be established as heir, Empress Wu asked Fuyuan; he firmly declared it impossible, and was therefore slandered to death by Chengsi—the empire considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Jiafu and others asked that Wu Chengsi be made heir, Empress Wu consulted Fuyuan, who firmly declared it impossible. Chengsi then slandered him to his death, and the empire regarded it as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 輔元兄希元，高宗時洛州司法參軍，章懷太子召令與洗馬劉訥言等註解范曄《後漢書》，行於代。

translations.literal: Fuyuan's elder brother Xiyuan, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, was Legal Assistant in Luozhou; Crown Prince Zhanghuai summoned him to join Palace Steward Liu Nayan and others in annotating Fan Ye's 《Book of the Later Han》, which circulated in its age.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan's elder brother Xiyuan served under Emperor Gaozong as legal assistant in Luozhou. Crown Prince Zhanghuai summoned him to join palace steward Liu Nayan and others in annotating Fan Ye's 《Book of the Later Han》, which circulated widely in their day.

sentences.zh: 先輔元卒。

translations.literal: He died before Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 杜正倫，相州洹水人也。

translations.literal: Du Zhenglun was a native of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun was a native of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，與兄正玄、正藏俱以秀才擢第。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era of Sui, together with his elder brothers Zhengxuan and Zhengcang he all passed the Presented Scholar examination.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Renshou era he and his elder brothers Zhengxuan and Zhengcang all passed the Presented Scholar examination.

sentences.zh: 隋代舉秀才止十餘人，正倫一家有三秀才，甚為當時稱美。

translations.literal: In the Sui dynasty only a dozen or so men were selected as Presented Scholars; Zhenglun's household alone had three, which was greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui times only a dozen or so men were chosen as presented scholars; the Zhenglun household alone produced three, a feat much admired in their day.

sentences.zh: 正倫善屬文，深明釋典。

translations.literal: Zhenglun was skilled at literary composition and deeply versed in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was skilled at literary composition and deeply versed in Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為羽騎尉。

translations.literal: Serving Sui, he was a Feathered Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he served as a feathered cavalry guard.

sentences.zh: 武德中，歷遷齊州總管府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he rose through successive posts to Registrar in the Area Command of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he rose through successive posts to registrar in the area command of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，令直秦府文學館。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard his name and ordered him posted to the Literary Hall of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of him, he had him posted to the Literary Hall of the Prince of Qin's mansion.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，尚書右丞魏徵表薦正倫，以為古今難匹，遂擢授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Vice Director of the Left Department of the Ministry of State Wei Zheng memorialized recommending Zhenglun, declaring him unmatched in past or present; he was thereupon promoted and appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Wei Zheng, vice director of the left department of the Ministry of State, recommended Zhenglun as a man without equal in any age, and he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「朕今令舉行能之人，非朕獨私於行能者，以其能益於百姓也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to him: "I now order the selection of men of conduct and ability—not because I favor such men for my own sake alone, but because their ability can benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told him, "I am now promoting men of conduct and ability—not because I favor such men for my own sake, but because their ability can benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 朕於宗親及以勳舊無行能者，終不任之。

translations.literal: As for my kinsmen and meritorious elders who lack conduct and ability, I will never appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and old companions who lack conduct and ability—I will never appoint them.

sentences.zh: 以卿忠直，朕今舉卿，卿宜勉稱所舉。」

translations.literal: Because you are loyal and upright, I now promote you; you should strive to live up to what has been recommended in you.
translations.idiomatic: Because you are loyal and upright, I promote you now. You must strive to prove worthy of the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜給事中，兼知起居注。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Palace Gentry Attendant and concurrently placed in charge of the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed palace gentry attendant and placed in charge of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍臣曰：「朕每日坐朝，欲出一言，即思此言於百姓有利益否，所以不能多言。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once said to his attending ministers: "Each day when I hold court, whenever I wish to speak a word, I first consider whether that word will benefit the common people—therefore I cannot speak much.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once told his attending ministers, "Each day in court, before I speak I ask whether my words will benefit the people. That is why I speak so little.

sentences.zh: 正倫進曰：「君舉必書，言存左右史。

translations.literal: Zhenglun stepped forward and said: "The ruler's actions are always recorded; his words are kept by the left and right historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun stepped forward and said, "A ruler's every act is recorded; his words are kept by the left and right historiographers.

sentences.zh: 臣職當修起居注，不敢不盡愚直。

translations.literal: My duty is to compile the Daily Records; I dare not fail to offer all my blunt honesty.
translations.idiomatic: It is my duty to keep the Daily Records, and I dare not withhold my plainest counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下若一言乖於道理，則千載累於聖德，非直當今損於百姓，願陛下慎之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty speaks one word contrary to reason, it will burden your sacred virtue for a thousand ages—not merely harm the common people in the present; I beg Your Majesty to be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty speaks one word against reason, it will stain your sacred virtue for a thousand years—not merely harm the people today. I beg Your Majesty to be careful.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，賜絹二百段。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he rose through successive posts to vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，正倫與御史大夫韋挺、秘書少監虞世南、著作郎姚思廉等咸上封事稱旨，太宗為之設宴，因謂曰：「朕歷觀自古人臣立忠之事，若值明王，便得盡誠規諫，至如龍逢、比干，竟不免孥戮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zhenglun together with Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shinan, Director of the Bureau of Compilation Yao Silian, and others all submitted sealed memorials that pleased the emperor. Emperor Taizong held a feast for them and therefore said: "I have reviewed through the ages how ministers established loyalty: if they met an enlightened ruler, they could offer their full honest remonstrance; yet men like Longfeng and Bi Gan still could not escape execution along with their families.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhenglun, together with censor-in-chief Wei Ting, vice director of the Secretariat Yu Shinan, director of the Bureau of Compilation Yao Silian, and others, submitted sealed memorials that pleased the emperor. Taizong held a feast for them and said, "I have read how ministers through the ages gave loyal service: when they met an enlightened ruler they could remonstrate with full honesty—yet even Longfeng and Bi Gan were not spared execution along with their families.

sentences.zh: 為君不易，為臣極難。

translations.literal: To be a ruler is not easy; to be a minister is extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To be a ruler is not easy; to be a minister is exceedingly hard.

sentences.zh: 我又聞龍可擾而馴，然喉下有逆鱗，觸之則殺人。

translations.literal: I have also heard that a dragon may be tamed and made docile, yet beneath its throat there is a reverse scale—touch it and it kills.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a dragon can be tamed and made tractable, yet beneath its throat lies a reverse scale—touch it, and it kills.

sentences.zh: 人主亦有逆鱗，卿等遂不避犯觸，各進封事。

translations.literal: A sovereign too has a reverse scale; yet you did not shrink from touching it, each submitting a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign too has his reverse scale, yet you did not shrink from touching it—each of you submitted a sealed memorial.

sentences.zh: 常能如此，朕豈慮有危亡哉！

translations.literal: If you can always be like this, how should I worry over peril and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: If you can always be like this, why should I fear ruin!

sentences.zh: 我思卿等此意，豈能暫忘？

translations.literal: When I think of this intent of yours, how could I forget it even for a moment?
translations.idiomatic: When I think of what you have done, how could I forget it even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 故聊設宴樂也。」

translations.literal: Therefore I have merely set out this feast and music.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have set out this feast and music.

sentences.zh: 仍並賜帛有差。

translations.literal: He also granted each of them silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted each of them silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，行太子右庶子，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional post of Regular Attendant, acting as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and concurrently made a Scholar of the Hall of Venerating Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional post of regular attendant, served as acting right assistant to the heir apparent, and was made a scholar of the Hall of Venerating Worthies.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「國之儲副，自古所重，必擇善人為之輔佐。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to him: "The heir to the state has been valued since antiquity; one must choose good men to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told him, "The heir to the state has been valued since antiquity, and good men must be chosen to assist him.

sentences.zh: 今太子年在幼沖，志意未定，朕若朝夕見之，可得隨事誡約。

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince is still young and his will is unsettled; if I saw him morning and evening, I could admonish and restrain him as occasions arose.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is still young and his mind is unsettled. If I saw him morning and evening, I could counsel and restrain him as occasions arose.

sentences.zh: 今既委以監國，不在目前，知卿志懷貞愨，能敦直道，故輒輟卿於朕，以匡太子，宜知委任輕重也。」

translations.literal: Now that he has been entrusted with overseeing the state and is no longer before my eyes, knowing that your intent is upright and sincere and that you can uphold the straight path, I therefore take you from my side to guide the Crown Prince—you should understand the weight of this commission.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been entrusted with overseeing the state and is no longer before my eyes, knowing your intent to be upright and sincere and that you can uphold the straight path, I take you from my side to guide the crown prince. You should understand how weighty this commission is.

sentences.zh: 十年，復授中書侍郎，賜爵南陽縣侯，仍兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang County, and still concurrently served as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as marquis of Nanyang County, and still served concurrently as left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 正倫出入兩宮，參典機密，甚以干理稱。

translations.literal: Zhenglun moved between the two palaces, participated in confidential affairs, and was greatly praised for his practical competence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun moved between the two palaces, took part in confidential affairs, and was much praised for his practical competence.

sentences.zh: 時太子承乾有足疾，不能朝謁，好暱近群小。

translations.literal: At the time the Crown Prince Chenggan had an ailment of the foot and could not attend court audiences; he liked to draw close to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Crown Prince Chenggan had a foot ailment and could not attend court audiences; he liked to keep company with petty men.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂正倫曰：「我兒疾病，乃可事也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Zhenglun: "My son's illness is a tolerable matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told Zhenglun, "My son's illness is a tolerable matter.

sentences.zh: 但全無令譽，不聞愛賢好善，私所引接，多是小人，卿可察之。

translations.literal: But he has no fine reputation at all; I hear nothing of love for the worthy or delight in good; those he privately draws near are mostly petty men—you should watch this.
translations.idiomatic: But he has no fine reputation at all. I hear nothing of love for the worthy or delight in good; those he privately keeps near are mostly petty men. You must keep watch.

sentences.zh: 若教示不得，須來告我。」

translations.literal: If instruction and guidance fail, you must come and tell me.
translations.idiomatic: If instruction fails, you must come and tell me.

sentences.zh: 正倫數諫不納，乃以太宗語告之，承乾抗表聞奏。

translations.literal: Zhenglun remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded; he therefore told Chenggan the emperor's words, and Chenggan submitted a defiant memorial reporting this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded; he then told Chenggan what the emperor had said, and Chenggan submitted a defiant memorial reporting the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂正倫曰：「何故漏洩我語？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to Zhenglun: "Why did you leak my words?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said to Zhenglun, "Why did you leak my words?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「開導不入，故以陛下語嚇之，冀其有懼，或當反善。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Guidance would not enter, so I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping he would feel fear and perhaps turn back to good.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Counsel would not enter, so I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping he would feel fear and perhaps turn back to good.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出為谷州刺史，又左授交州都督。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent him out as Prefect of Gu Province; he was further demoted to Area Commander of Jiao Region.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent him out as prefect of Gu Province, then demoted him further to area commander of Jiao Region.

sentences.zh: 後承乾構逆，事與侯君集相連，稱遣君集將金帶遺正倫，由是配流驩州。

translations.literal: Later, when Chenggan plotted treason, the affair was linked with Hou Junji; it was said that Chenggan had sent Junji to present a gold belt to Zhenglun, and for this Zhenglun was sentenced to exile in Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chenggan plotted treason, the affair was linked with Hou Junji. It was said that Chenggan had sent Junji to present a gold belt to Zhenglun, and for this Zhenglun was sentenced to exile in Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，累授黃門侍郎，兼崇賢館學士，尋同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he rose through successive appointments to Vice Director of the Gate, concurrently a Scholar of the Hall of Venerating Worthies, and soon Third Rank, Participating with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he rose through successive appointments to vice director of the Gate, concurrently a scholar of the Hall of Venerating Worthies, and soon third rank, participating with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼度支尚書，仍依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently served as Minister of Revenue and still continued to participate in state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he concurrently served as minister of revenue while continuing to participate in state affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書令，兼太子賓客、弘文館學士，進封襄陽縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary, concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent and Scholar of the Hall for Advancing Literature, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xiangyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed grand secretary, concurrently guest of the heir apparent and scholar of the Hall for Advancing Literature, and advanced in enfeoffment to duke of Xiangyang County.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐與中書令李義府不協，出為橫州刺史，仍削其封邑。

translations.literal: In the third year, for discord with Grand Secretary Li Yifu, he was sent out as Prefect of Heng Prefecture, and his fief was still reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, for falling out with Grand Secretary Li Yifu, he was sent out as prefect of Heng Prefecture and his fief was reduced.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 有集十捲行於代。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in ten scroll volumes that circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, in ten scroll volumes, circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王珪履正不回，忠讜無比，君臣時命，胥會於茲。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Wang Gui walked upright and never turned aside; his loyalty and forthrightness were without parallel—ruler and minister, timing and fate, all met in this.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wang Gui walked upright and never swerved; his loyalty and forthrightness were without parallel—ruler and minister, timing and destiny, all converged here.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「自天祐之，吉無不利。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Blessed by Heaven, good fortune—nothing unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Heaven's blessing brings good fortune without fail.

sentences.zh: 叔玠有焉。

translations.literal: Shujie had this.
translations.idiomatic: In Shujie this was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 戴胄兩朝仕官，一乃心力，刑無僭濫，事有箴規。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou served as an official through two reigns with single-minded devotion; in punishments there was no excess, and in affairs there was admonition and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou served through two reigns with single-minded devotion: punishments knew no excess, and in affairs he offered counsel and restraint.

sentences.zh: 雖學術不能求備，而匡益自可濟時，亦所謂巧於任大矣。

translations.literal: Although his learning could not be made complete, his corrective benefit could still aid the age—this too is what is called skill in bearing great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Though his learning could not be made complete, the good he did could still serve the age—this too is what is meant by skill in bearing great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 文本文傾江海，忠貫雪霜，申慈父之冤，匡明主之業，及委繁劇，俄致暴終。

translations.literal: Wenben's prose rivaled rivers and seas; his loyalty pierced frost and snow. He vindicated his affectionate father's wrong, upheld the enlightened sovereign's enterprise—and once entrusted with heavy and urgent duties, soon met a sudden end.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's prose rivaled rivers and seas; his loyalty pierced frost and snow. He vindicated his affectionate father's wrong, upheld the enlightened sovereign's enterprise—and once burdened with heavy and urgent duties, he soon met a sudden end.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「小心翼翼，昭事上帝。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Be cautious and careful; clearly serve the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Be cautious and careful in serving the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 所謂憂能傷人，不復永年矣。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by saying that worry can harm a man—he did not again reach old age.
translations.idiomatic: So it is said that worry can wear a man down—he did not live to old age.

sentences.zh: 洎羲而下，登清要者數十人。

translations.literal: Down from Xi, several dozen reached prestigious posts.
translations.idiomatic: From Xi downward, several dozen kinsmen reached prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 積善之道，焉可忽諸？

translations.literal: The way of accumulating good—how can it be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: The way of accumulating good—how can it be neglected?

sentences.zh: 正倫以能文被舉，以直道見委，參典機密，出入兩宮，斯謂得時。

translations.literal: Zhenglun was recommended for his literary ability, entrusted for his upright path, participated in confidential affairs, and moved between the two palaces—this is called finding the right time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was promoted for his literary talent, entrusted for his upright conduct, took part in confidential affairs, and moved between the two palaces—this was finding his moment.

sentences.zh: 然被承乾金帶之譏，孰與夫薏苡之謗，士大夫慎之。

translations.literal: Yet he suffered the slander of Chenggan's gold belt—how does that compare with the calumny of barley seed? Gentlemen should be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he fell under the shadow of Chenggan's gold belt—what difference from the calumny of barley seed? Let gentlemen take heed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：五靈嘉瑞，出系汙隆。

translations.literal: Eulogy: The five divine auspicious portents emerge bound to rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: The five divine auspicious portents appear tied to the rise and fall of the age.

sentences.zh: 人中麟鳳，王、戴諸公。

translations.literal: Unicorn and phoenix among men—Lords Wang, Dai, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Unicorns and phoenixes among men—Lords Wang, Dai, and their fellows.

sentences.zh: 動必由禮，言皆匡躬。

translations.literal: In action they always followed ritual; in speech they all corrected themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In action they always followed ritual; in speech they always corrected themselves.

sentences.zh: 獻規納諫，貞觀之風。

translations.literal: Offering counsel and accepting remonstrance—the spirit of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Offering counsel and accepting remonstrance—the spirit of the Zhenguan reign.
